Volume 244 Biographies 132: Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, Wei Dazhong, Zhou Chaorui, Yuan Huazhong, Gu Dazhang, Wang Zhicai

1
杨涟，字文孺，应山人。 为人磊落负奇节。 万历三十五年成进士，除常熟知县。 举廉吏第一，擢户科给事中，转兵科右给事中。
Yang Lian, whose style name was Wenru, came from Yingshan. He was open-hearted and upright, possessed of rare moral courage. In the thirty-fifth year of the Wanli reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Changshu. Named the foremost incorrupt official, he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Household Bureau and later transferred to right supervising secretary in the Military Bureau.
2
四十八年，神宗疾，不食且半月，皇太子未得见。 涟偕诸给事、御史走谒大学士方从哲，御史左光斗趣从哲问安。 从哲曰：“帝讳疾。 即问左右，不敢传。 ”涟曰：“昔文潞公问宋仁宗疾，内侍不肯言。 潞公曰：‘天子起居，汝曹不令宰相知，将毋有他志，速下中书行法。 ’公诚日三问，不必见，亦不必上知，第令宫中知廷臣在，事自济。 公更当宿阁中。 ”曰：“无故事。 ”涟曰：“潞公不诃史志聪，此何时，尚问故事耶？ ”越二日，从哲始率廷臣入问。 及帝疾亟，太子尚踌躇宫门外。 涟、光斗遣人语东宫伴读王安：“帝疾甚，不召太子，非帝意。 当力请入侍，尝药视膳，薄暮始还。 ”太子深纳之。
In the forty-eighth year of his reign the Shenzong Emperor fell gravely ill and went nearly half a month without eating, yet the crown prince was still not allowed to see him. Lian hurried off with the other supervising secretaries and censors to see Grand Secretary Fang Congzhe, while Censor Zuo Guangdou pressed Congzhe to ask after the emperor's condition. Congzhe said, "The emperor does not wish his illness spoken of. Even if you ask those at his side, they will not dare pass the word along." Lian replied, "Long ago, when Duke Wen of Lu asked after Emperor Renzong of Song's illness, the palace attendants refused to answer. The duke said, 'The sovereign's daily condition—if you will not let the chief minister know of it, might you not harbor some other intent? Send the matter down at once to the Central Secretariat to be handled according to law.' If you, sir, were to inquire three times a day, you need not see him yourself, nor need the emperor even know of it—only let the palace know that officials of the court are present, and things will right themselves. You ought moreover to stay the night in the privy council hall." Congzhe said, "There is no precedent for that." Lian said, "The duke did not hesitate to rebuke Shi Zhicong—what moment is this, and you are still asking about precedent?" Two days later Congzhe at last led the court officials in to inquire after the emperor. When the emperor's illness turned grave, the crown prince still hesitated outside the palace gate. Lian and Guangdou sent word to Wang An, reader-in-waiting to the eastern palace: "The emperor is gravely ill. If he has not summoned the crown prince, that is not the emperor's true wish. Press hard to gain admission to attend him, taste his medicines, and oversee his meals, and do not return until evening." The crown prince took the advice deeply to heart.
3
无何，神宗崩。 八月丙午朔，光宗嗣位。 越四日，不豫。 都人喧言郑贵妃进美姬八人，又使中官崔文升投以利剂，帝一昼夜三四十起。 而是时，贵妃据乾清宫，与帝所宠李选侍相结，贵妃为选侍请皇后封，选侍亦请封贵妃为皇太后。 帝外家王、郭二戚畹，遍谒朝士，泣朔宫禁危状，谓：“帝疾必不起，文升药故也，非误也。 郑、李交甚固，包藏祸心。 ”廷臣闻其语，忧甚。 而帝果趣礼部封贵妃为皇太后。 涟、光斗乃倡言于朝，共诘责郑养性，令贵妃移宫，贵妃即移慈宁。 涟遂劾崔文升用药无状，请推问之。 且曰：“外廷流言，谓陛下兴居无节，侍御蛊惑。 必文升藉口以掩其用药之奸，文升之党煽布以预杜外廷之口。 既损圣躬，又亏圣德，罪不容死。 至贵妃封号，尤乖典常。 尊以嫡母，若大行皇后何？ 尊以生母，若本生太后何？ 请亟寝前命。 ”疏上，越三日丁卯，帝召见大臣，并及涟，且宣锦衣官校。 众谓涟疏忤旨，必廷杖，嘱从哲为解。 从哲劝涟引罪，涟抗声曰：“死即死耳，涟何罪？ ”及入，帝温言久之，数目涟，语外廷毋信流言。 遂逐文升，停封太后命。 再召大臣皆及涟。
Before long the Shenzong Emperor died. On the first day of the intercalary sixth month of the eighth year, Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne. Four days later he fell ill. Rumors spread through the capital that Consort Zheng had sent in eight beautiful women and had the eunuch Cui Wensheng give the emperor an aphrodisiac, so that he rose twenty or thirty times in a single day and night. At that time the consort held Qianqing Palace and had joined forces with Lady Li, whom the emperor favored; the consort sought empress rank for Lady Li, while Lady Li in turn sought to have the consort made empress dowager. The emperor's maternal relatives, the Wang and Guo families, went from one court official to another in tears, describing the danger within the palace walls: "The emperor will not recover; it is because of Wensheng's medicine, not by accident. Zheng and Li are tightly bound together and harbor malicious intent." When court officials heard this, their alarm was great. The emperor in fact pressed the Ministry of Rites to grant the consort the title of empress dowager. Lian and Guangdou then spoke out in court, jointly confronting Zheng Yangxing and demanding that the consort vacate her palace; she promptly moved to Cining. Lian then impeached Cui Wensheng for improper administration of medicine and called for a full investigation. He also wrote, "Rumors outside the court claim that Your Majesty's daily conduct lacks restraint and that your attendants have led you astray. Surely Wensheng seizes on such talk to conceal his crime in administering medicine, while his faction spreads these rumors in advance to silence criticism from outside the court. He has harmed the emperor's person and tarnished his moral standing; his offense deserves death without mercy. As for granting the consort her title, that is especially contrary to established precedent. If she is honored as the principal mother, what becomes of the late empress? If she is honored as the birth mother, what becomes of the emperor's own birth mother? I beg that the previous order be withdrawn at once." After the memorial went up, three days later on the day dingmao the emperor summoned the chief ministers, Lian included, and also sent for officers of the Embroidered Uniform Guard. Everyone believed Lian's memorial had defied the throne and that he would surely be beaten at court; they urged Congzhe to plead on his behalf. Congzhe urged Lian to confess fault, but Lian answered boldly, "If I must die, then die I shall—what crime have I committed?" When he entered, the emperor spoke to him at length in a gentle tone, looked at him several times, and told those outside the court not to credit idle rumors. He then expelled Wensheng and suspended the order granting the empress dowager her title. Each time the chief ministers were summoned thereafter, Lian was included.
4
涟自以小臣预顾命感激，誓以死报。 九月乙亥朔，昧爽，帝崩。 廷臣趋入，诸大臣周嘉谟、张问达、李汝华等虑皇长子无嫡母、生母，势孤孑甚，欲共托之李选侍。 涟曰：“天子宁可托妇人？ 且选侍昨于先帝召对群臣时，强上入，复推之出，是岂可托幼主者？ 请亟见储皇，即呼万岁，拥出乾清，暂居慈庆。 ”语未毕，大学士方从哲、刘一燝、韩爌至，涟趣诸大臣共趋乾清宫。 阍人持梃不容入，涟大骂：“奴才！ 皇帝召我等。 今已晏驾，若曹不听入，欲何为！ ”阍人却，乃入临。 群臣呼万岁，请于初六日登极，而奉驾至文华殿，受群臣嵩呼。 驾甫至中宫，内竖从寝阁出，大呼：“拉少主何往？ 主年少畏人！ ”有揽衣欲夺还者。 涟格而诃之曰：“殿下群臣之主，四海九州莫非臣子，复畏何人！ ”乃拥至文华殿。 礼毕，奉驾入慈庆宫。 当是时，李选侍居乾清。 一燝奏曰：“殿下暂居此，俟选侍出宫讫，乃归乾清宫。 ”群臣遂退议登极期，语纷纷未定，有请改初三者，有请于即日午时者。 涟曰：“今海宇清晏，内无嫡庶之嫌。 父死之谓何？ 含敛未毕，衮冕临朝，非礼也。 ”或言登极则人心安，涟曰：“安与不安，不在登极早暮。 处之得宜，即朝委裘何害？ ”议定，出过文华殿。 太仆少卿徐养量、御史左光斗至，责涟误大事，唾其面曰：“事脱不济，汝死，肉足食乎！ ”涟为竦然。 乃与光斗从周嘉谟于朝房，言选侍无恩德，必不可同居。
Lian himself, deeply moved that a minor official had been included in the deathbed charge, swore to repay the trust with his life. On the first day of the ninth month, at daybreak, the emperor died. Court officials rushed in. Chief ministers Zhou Jiamo, Zhang Wenda, Li Ruhua, and others, fearing that the eldest imperial son lacked both a principal mother and a birth mother and stood utterly alone, wished to place him jointly in the care of Lady Li, the attendant consort. Lian said, "Can the Son of Heaven be entrusted to a woman? Moreover, when the late emperor summoned the court yesterday, the attendant consort forced her way in and then pushed him out again—is this someone fit to guard a young sovereign? Let us see the heir at once, cry 'Long live the emperor!' immediately, escort him out of Qianqing Palace, and lodge him temporarily at Ciqing." Before he had finished, Grand Secretaries Fang Congzhe, Liu Yijin, and Han Kuang arrived, and Lian urged all the chief ministers to hurry together to Qianqing Palace. Gatekeepers armed with clubs barred the way; Lian shouted, "You slaves! The emperor summoned us. He is already dead—if you will not let us in, what do you intend!" The gatekeepers fell back, and they entered to mourn the deceased emperor. The officials cried 'Long live the emperor!' and asked that enthronement take place on the sixth; they then escorted the heir to Wenhua Hall, where the officials received him with shouts of homage. The carriage had scarcely reached the central palace when eunuchs emerged from the sleeping quarters and shouted, "Where are you dragging the young lord? The lord is young and afraid of strangers!" Some seized his robes, trying to pull him back. Lian blocked them and rebuked them: "Your Highness is lord to all the officials; throughout the realm there is none who is not his subject—whom need he fear!" They then escorted him to Wenhua Hall. When the rites were complete, they escorted him into Ciqing Palace. At that time Lady Li, the attendant consort, still occupied Qianqing Palace. Yijin said, "Your Highness will stay here for the time being; when the attendant consort has left the palace, you may return to Qianqing Palace." The officials then withdrew to debate the date of enthronement; opinions flew back and forth without resolution—some wanted the third, others wanted noon that very day. Lian said, "The realm is at peace, and within the palace there is no strife between principal and secondary heirs. What does it mean that one's father has just died? The encoffining is not yet complete, yet to don the imperial regalia and hold court would be contrary to ritual." Some argued that enthronement would settle people's minds; Lian replied, "Whether minds are settled depends not on enthronement being early or late. If matters are handled properly, what harm is there in holding court while still in mourning robes?" Once the matter was settled, they left Wenhua Hall. Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Xu Yangliang and Censor Zuo Guangdou arrived, rebuked Lian for jeopardizing a critical matter, spat in his face, and said, "If this fails, even your death will not be enough to atone!" Lian was startled. He then went with Guangdou to join Zhou Jiamo in the court chamber and argued that the attendant consort had shown no grace or virtue and must by no means remain with the heir.
5
明日，嘉谟、光斗各上疏请选侍移宫。 初四日得俞旨。 而选侍听李进忠计，必欲皇长子同居，恶光斗疏中“武氏”语，议召皇长子，加光斗重谴。 涟遇内竖于麟趾门，内竖备言状。 涟正色曰：“殿下在东宫为太子，今则为皇帝，选侍安得召？ 且上已十六岁，他日即不奈选侍何，若曹置身何地？ ”怒目视之，其人退。 给事中惠世扬、御史张泼入东宫门，骇相告曰：“选侍欲垂帘处光斗，汝等何得晏然？ ”涟曰：“无之。 ”出皇极门，九卿科道议上公疏，未决。
The next day Jiamo and Guangdou each submitted memorials calling for the attendant consort to vacate the palace. On the fourth they received the emperor's assent. But the attendant consort, following Li Jinzhong's advice, insisted that the eldest imperial son remain with her; resenting Guangdou's reference in his memorial to "the Wu clan," she planned to summon the heir and impose severe punishment on Guangdou. Lian met an inner eunuch at Linzhi Gate, who gave him a full account of what was afoot. Lian said sternly, "Your Highness was crown prince in the eastern palace; now he is emperor—how can the attendant consort summon him? Moreover, His Majesty is already sixteen; even if one day he cannot prevail against the attendant consort, where will you stand then?" He glared at the man angrily, and the eunuch withdrew. Supervising Secretary Hui Shiyang and Censor Zhang Po entered the eastern palace gate and, alarmed, told one another, "The attendant consort means to sit behind the curtain and punish Guangdou—how can you remain at ease?" Lian said, "Nothing of the kind." They went out through Huangji Gate; the Nine Ministers and the supervising secretaries and censors debated submitting a joint memorial from the chief ministers, but could not agree.
6
初五日传闻欲缓移宫期。 涟及诸大臣毕集慈庆宫门外，涟语从哲趣之。 从哲曰：“迟亦无害。 ”涟曰：“昨以皇长子就太子宫犹可，明日为天子，乃反居太子宫以避宫人乎？ 即两宫圣母如在，夫死亦当从子。 选侍何人，敢欺藐如此！ ”时中官往来如织，或言选侍亦顾命中人。 涟斥之曰：“诸臣受顾命于先帝，先帝自欲先顾其子，何尝先顾其嬖媵？ 请选侍于九庙前质之，若曹岂食李家禄者？ 能杀我则已，否则，今日不移死不去。 ”一燝、嘉谟助之，词色俱厉，声彻御前。 皇长子使使宣谕，乃退。 复抗疏言：“选侍阳托保护之名，阴图专擅之实，宫必不可不移。 臣言之在今日，殿下行之在今日，诸大臣赞决之，亦惟今日。 ”其日，选侍遂移宫，居仁寿殿。 明日庚辰，熹宗即位。 自光宗崩，至是凡六日。 涟与一燝、嘉谟定宫府危疑，言官惟光斗助之，余悉听涟指。 涟须发尽白，帝亦数称忠臣，未几，迁兵科都给事中。 御史冯三元等极诋熊廷弼，涟疏谕其事，独持平。 旋劾兵部尚书黄嘉善八大罪，嘉善罢去。
On the fifth rumors spread that the move would be postponed. Lian and the chief ministers all gathered outside Ciqing Palace, and Lian urged Congzhe to press the matter. Congzhe said, "A little delay does no harm." Lian said, "Yesterday it was still acceptable for the eldest imperial son to stay in the heir apparent's palace; tomorrow he becomes emperor—will he then live in the heir apparent's palace to avoid palace women?" Even if both empress dowagers of the two palaces were still alive, when the husband dies the wife should follow the son. Who is this attendant consort, that she dares treat us with such contempt!" Eunuchs came and went in a constant stream; some said the attendant consort too had been named in the deathbed charge. Lian rebuked them: "We officials received the deathbed charge from the late emperor; the late emperor wished first to care for his son—when did he ever wish first to care for his favorite concubine? Bring the attendant consort before the imperial ancestral temple and confront her there—are you people those who eat the Li family's stipends?" If you can kill me, then do so; otherwise, if she does not move today, I will not leave even at the cost of my life. Yijin and Jiamo supported him; their words and bearing were fierce alike, and their voices reached the throne. The eldest imperial son sent a messenger with an imperial pronouncement, and they withdrew. He submitted another forceful memorial: "The attendant consort outwardly claims protection while inwardly plotting exclusive control; she must vacate the palace without fail. What I say must be done today; what Your Highness does must be done today; what the chief ministers approve must be done today and today alone." That same day the attendant consort moved out and took up residence in Renshou Hall. The next day, on the day gengchen, Emperor Xizong ascended the throne. From Emperor Guangzong's death until this point six days had passed in all. Lian worked with Liu Yijin and Zhou Jiamo to resolve the palace and court crisis; of the remonstrating officials only Zuo Guangdou backed them, while all the rest followed Lian's lead. Lian's hair and beard had turned completely white; the emperor repeatedly praised him as a loyal minister, and before long he was promoted to chief supervising secretary in the Military Bureau. When Censor Feng Sanyuan and others fiercely attacked Xiong Tingbi, Lian submitted a memorial clarifying the affair, alone taking a balanced position. He soon impeached Minister of War Huang Jiashan on eight major charges, and Jiashan was removed from office.
7
当选侍之移宫也，涟即言于诸大臣曰：“选侍不移宫，非所以尊天子。 既移宫，又当有以安选侍。 是在诸公调护，无使中官取快私仇。 ”既而诸奄果为流言。 御史贾继春遂上书内阁，谓不当于新君御极之初，首劝主上以违忤先帝，逼逐庶母，表里交构，罗织不休，俾先帝玉体未寒，遂不能保一姬女。 盖是时，选侍宫奴刘逊、刘朝、田诏等以盗宝系狱，词连选侍父。 诸奄计无所出，则妄言选侍投缳，皇八妹入井，以荧惑朝士。 继春藉其言，首发难。 于是光斗上疏述移宫事。 而帝降谕言选侍气殴圣母，及要挟传封皇后，与即日欲垂帘听政语，又言：“今奉养李氏于哕鸾宫，尊敬不敢怠。 ”大学士从哲封还上谕。 帝复降谕言选侍过恶，而自白赡养优厚，俾廷臣知。 未几，哕鸾宫灾。 帝谕内阁，言选侍暨皇八妹无恙。 而是时，给事中周朝瑞谓继春生事，继春与相诋諆，乃复上书内阁，有：“伶仃之皇八妹，入井谁怜； 孀寡之未亡人，雉经莫诉”语。 朝瑞与辨驳者再。 涟恐继春说遂滋，亦上《敬述移宫始末疏》，且言：“选侍自裁，皇八妹入井，蜚语何自，臣安敢无言。 臣宁使今日忤选侍，无宁使移宫不速，不幸而成女后独览文书、称制垂帘之事。 ”帝优诏褒涟志安社稷，复降谕备述宫掖情事。 继春及其党益忌涟，诋涟结王安，图封拜。 涟不胜愤，冬十二月抗章乞去，即出城候命。 帝复褒其忠直而许之归。 天启元年春，继春按江西还，抵家，见帝诸谕，乃具疏陈上书之实。 帝切责，罢其官。 涟、继春先后去，移宫论始息。
When the attendant consort was to be moved from the palace, Lian told the chief ministers at once: "If the attendant consort does not leave the palace, that is no way to honor the Son of Heaven. Once she has moved out, there must also be some way to reassure the attendant consort. That is for you gentlemen to manage with care, and not to let eunuchs settle private scores. "Before long the eunuchs did spread malicious rumors. Censor Jia Jichun then wrote to the Grand Secretariat, arguing that at the very start of the new emperor's reign they should not have been the first to urge the sovereign to defy the late emperor, hound away a stepmother, conspire inside and outside the court, and pile on accusations without end—so that while the late emperor's body was not yet cold, not even one concubine daughter could be kept safe. At that time the attendant consort's palace servants Liu Xun, Liu Chao, Tian Zhao, and others were imprisoned for stealing treasures, and their testimony implicated her father. The eunuchs, at their wits' end, then spread false reports that the attendant consort had hanged herself and that the emperor's eighth sister had thrown herself into a well, hoping to unsettle the court. Jichun seized on these rumors and was the first to launch the attack. Guangdou then submitted a memorial recounting the whole move-palace affair. The emperor issued an edict stating that the attendant consort had violently assaulted the empress dowager, demanded to be made empress, and had even spoken of holding court from behind a curtain that very day; he also said, "Lady Li is now maintained at Huanyuan Palace, and I treat her with respect and never neglect her. "Grand Secretary Fang Congzhe returned the edict unopened. The emperor issued another edict detailing the attendant consort's wrongdoing while insisting that his care for her had been generous, so the court would understand. Before long Huanyuan Palace burned down. The emperor told the Grand Secretariat that the attendant consort and the emperor's eighth sister were safe and unharmed. At that time Supervising Secretary Zhou Chaorui accused Jichun of stirring up trouble; the two traded accusations, and Jichun again wrote to the Grand Secretariat with the lines: "The lonely imperial eighth sister—thrown into a well, who will pity her? The widowed woman not yet dead—who will hear her cry of the hanging noose?" Chaorui rebutted him twice. Fearing that Jichun's claims would spread, Lian also submitted his "Memorial Respectfully Recounting the Move-Palace Affair from Beginning to End," writing: "That the attendant consort killed herself and the imperial eighth sister went into a well—where did these slanders come from? How can your subject stay silent? Your subject would rather offend the attendant consort today than risk a delayed move from the palace and, by misfortune, see a woman ruler reviewing documents alone and holding power from behind the curtain." The emperor responded with a gracious edict praising Lian's devotion to the state's security, and issued another edict fully recounting affairs within the palace. Jichun and his allies grew even more hostile to Lian, accusing him of colluding with Wang An to win titles and promotion. Unable to bear the outrage, Lian submitted a forceful memorial requesting dismissal in the twelfth month, then left the city at once to await the emperor's reply. The emperor again praised his loyalty and integrity and allowed him to retire. In the spring of the first year of Tianqi, Jichun returned from his inspection tour of Jiangxi; when he reached home and read the emperor's edicts, he submitted a full memorial explaining what he had actually written. The emperor rebuked him severely and stripped him of office. After Lian and Jichun had both departed, the controversy over the move-palace affair finally died down.
8
天启二年起涟礼科都给事中，旋擢太常少卿。 明年冬，拜左佥都御史。 又明年春，进左副都御史。 而是时魏忠贤已用事，群小附之，惮众正盈朝，不敢大肆。 涟益与赵南星、左光斗、魏大中辈激扬讽议，务植善类，抑憸邪。 忠贤及其党衔次骨，遂兴汪文言狱，将罗织诸人。 事虽获解，然正人势日危。 其年六月，涟遂抗疏劾忠贤，列其二十四大罪，言：高皇帝定令，内官不许干预外事，只供掖廷洒扫，违者法无赦。 圣明在御，乃有肆无忌惮，浊乱朝常，如东厂太监魏忠贤者。 敢列其罪状，为陛下言之。
In the second year of Tianqi Lian was recalled as chief supervising secretary in the Rites Bureau, and was soon promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. The following winter he was appointed left vice censor-in-chief. The next spring he was promoted to left assistant censor-in-chief. By then Wei Zhongxian was already in control; petty men clustered around him, but with upright officials filling the court they did not yet dare act openly. Lian worked all the harder with Zhao Nanxing, Zuo Guangdou, Wei Dazhong, and others to rouse public criticism, striving to promote the good and restrain the wicked and sycophantic. Zhongxian and his faction hated them to the marrow and thereupon engineered the Wang Wenyan case, intending to entangle them all. Although the case was eventually resolved, the position of upright officials grew more precarious by the day. That sixth month Lian submitted a forceful memorial impeaching Zhongxian, listing twenty-four major crimes. He wrote: The founding emperor decreed that inner officials must not meddle in outside affairs and were only to attend to sweeping and cleaning in the inner palace; violators were to be punished without mercy. Yet under a sage sovereign on the throne there is one who acts with utter impunity and corrupts the normal order of government—the Eastern Depot eunuch Wei Zhongxian. I dare set out his crimes and lay them before Your Majesty.
9
忠贤本市井无赖，中年净身，夤入内地，初犹谬为小忠、小信以幸恩，继乃敢为大奸、大恶以乱政。 祖制，以拟旨专责阁臣。 自忠贤擅权，多出传奉，或径自内批，坏祖宗二百余年之政体，大罪一。
Zhongxian was originally a street ruffian who was castrated in middle age and slithered into the inner palace; at first he feigned petty loyalty and petty trustworthiness to win favor, then dared great treachery and great wickedness to corrupt the government. By ancestral institution, drafting imperial edicts was the exclusive duty of the grand secretaries. Since Zhongxian seized power, edicts have often been issued by direct transmission or approved straight from within the palace, destroying more than two hundred years of ancestral government—great crime one.
10
刘一燝、周嘉谟，顾命大臣也，忠贤令孙杰论去。 急于翦己之忌，不容陛下不改父之臣，大罪二。
Liu Yijin and Zhou Jiamo were ministers entrusted at the late emperor's deathbed; Zhongxian had Sun Jie impeach them and force them out. Eager to destroy those he resented, he would not allow Your Majesty to keep your father's ministers—great crime two.
11
先帝宾天，实有隐恨，孙慎行、邹元标以公义发愤，忠贤悉排去之。 顾于党护选侍之沈纮，曲意绸缪，终加蟒玉。 亲乱贼而仇忠义，大罪三。
When the late emperor died there was in truth hidden bitterness; Sun Shenxing and Zou Yuanbiao spoke out in righteous indignation, and Zhongxian drove them all away. Yet toward Shen Hong, who had factionally shielded the attendant consort, he showed deliberate favor and in the end granted him python robes and jade ornaments. Embracing traitors while treating the loyal and righteous as enemies—great crime three.
12
王纪、钟羽正先年功在国本。 及纪为司寇，执法如山； 羽正为司空，清修如鹤。 忠贤构党斥逐，必不容盛时有正色立朝之直臣，大罪四。
Wang Ji and Zhong Yuzheng had earlier rendered great service in securing the imperial succession. When Ji became Minister of Justice, he enforced the law with immovable firmness; when Yuzheng became Minister of Works, he lived with the purity of a crane. Zhongxian formed factions to expel them and would not tolerate upright ministers who could stand in court with stern integrity in a flourishing age—great crime four.
13
国家最重无如枚卜。 忠贤一手握定，力阻首推之孙慎行、盛以弘，更为他辞以锢其出。 岂真欲门生宰相乎？ 大罪五。
In the state nothing is more important than selecting the chief minister by lot. Zhongxian kept the process in his own grip, forcefully blocking the top candidates Sun Shenxing and Sheng Yihong and inventing other excuses to keep them out. Does he truly intend to install his own protégé as prime minister? Great crime five.
14
爵人于朝，莫重廷推。 去岁南太宰、北少宰皆用陪推，致一时名贤不安其位。 颠倒铨政，掉弄机权，大罪六。
In granting office at court, nothing is more important than collegiate recommendation. Last year both the southern grand director and northern vice director of the Ministry of Personnel were appointed through subsidiary recommendation, leaving eminent men of the day insecure in their posts. Distorting personnel policy and manipulating the machinery of power—great crime six.
15
圣政初新，正资忠直。 乃满朝荐、文震孟、熊德阳、江秉谦、徐大相、毛士龙、侯震旸等，抗论稍忤，立行贬黜，屡经恩典，竟阻赐环。 长安谓天子之怒易解，忠贤之怒难调，大罪七。
At the start of a sage reign, the court depends on loyal and forthright men. Yet Man Chaojian, Wen Zhenmeng, Xiong Deyang, Jiang Bingqian, Xu Daxiang, Mao Shilong, Hou Zhenyong, and others—because their forceful remonstrance gave slight offense—were dismissed at once; though imperial grace was repeatedly shown, they were ultimately barred from recall. People in the capital say the emperor's anger is easy to appease, but Zhongxian's anger is not—great crime seven.
16
然犹曰外廷臣子也。 去岁南郊之日，传闻宫中有一贵人，以德性贞静，荷上宠注。 忠贤恐其露己骄横，托言急病，置之死地。 是陛下不能保其贵幸矣，大罪八。
Yet one might still say these were only outer-court officials. On the day of last year's southern suburban sacrifice, rumor had it that there was a palace lady of virtuous and quiet character who enjoyed the emperor's favor. Zhongxian, fearing she would expose his arrogance, claimed she had taken sudden ill and had her killed. Thus Your Majesty could not even protect a woman you favored—great crime eight.
17
犹曰无名封也。 裕妃以有妊传封，中外方为庆幸。 忠贤恶其不附己，矫旨勒令自尽。 是陛下不能保其妃嫔矣，大罪九。
One might still say she held no formal title. Consort Yu, because she was pregnant, received an imperial enfeoffment, and court and country alike rejoiced. Zhongxian hated that she would not attach herself to him and forged an edict ordering her to kill herself. Thus Your Majesty could not even protect your own consorts—great crime nine.
18
犹曰在妃嫔也。 中宫有庆，已经成男，乃忽焉告殒，传闻忠贤与奉圣夫人实有谋焉。 是陛下且不能保其子矣，大罪十。
One might still say this concerned only consorts. The empress had good news and had already borne a son, yet suddenly came word that he had died; rumor held that Zhongxian and Lady Fengsheng had actually plotted it. Thus Your Majesty could not even protect your own child—great crime ten.
19
先帝青宫四十年，所与护持孤危者惟王安耳。 即陛下仓卒受命，拥卫防维，安亦不可谓无劳。 忠贤以私忿，矫旨杀于南苑。 是不但仇王安，而实敢仇先帝之老奴，况其他内臣无罪而擅杀擅逐者，又不知几千百也，大罪十一。
Throughout the late emperor's forty years as heir apparent, the one who stood by him and protected him in his lonely peril was Wang An alone. Even when Your Majesty hastily ascended the throne, Wang An cannot be said to have lacked merit in shielding and protecting you. Out of private resentment Zhongxian forged an edict and had him executed in the Southern Park. This was not merely to make an enemy of Wang An, but truly to dare make an enemy of the late emperor's old servant; not to mention the countless other inner officials guiltlessly killed or driven out at will—great crime eleven.
20
今日奖赏，明日祠额，要挟无穷，王言屡亵。 近又于河间毁人居屋，起建牌坊，镂凤雕龙，干云插汉，又不止茔地僭拟陵寝而已，大罪十二。
Rewards today, temple plaques tomorrow—endless extortion, and the emperor's words repeatedly debased. Recently in Hejian he demolished people's homes and erected a memorial arch carved with phoenixes and dragons, towering to the clouds—and this went beyond merely usurping an imperial tomb for his own burial ground—great crime twelve.
21
今日廕中书，明日廕锦衣。 金吾之堂口皆乳臭，诰敕之馆目不识丁。 如魏良弼、魏良材、魏良卿、魏希孔及其甥傅应星等，滥袭恩廕，亵越朝常，大罪十三。
Hereditary appointments to the Secretariat today, hereditary appointments to the Embroidered Uniform Guard tomorrow. The halls of the Golden Guard are filled with callow youths; in the Proclamation and Edict Office they cannot read a single character. Men such as Wei Liangbi, Wei Liangcai, Wei Liangqing, Wei Xikong, and his nephew Fu Yingxing and others have recklessly inherited privilege after privilege, trampling the normal order of court—great crime thirteen.
22
用立枷之法，戚畹家人骈首毕命，意欲诬陷国戚，动摇中宫。 若非阁臣力持，言官纠正，椒房之戚，又兴大狱矣，大罪十四。
Using the standing cangue, he caused members of imperial kinsmen's households to die one after another, intending to frame the imperial relatives and undermine the empress. Had the grand secretaries not forcefully resisted and the remonstrating officials not corrected the matter, a major case would have been raised against the empress's kin—great crime fourteen.
23
良乡生员章士魁，坐争煤窑，托言开矿而致之死。 假令盗长陵一抔土，何以处之？ 赵高鹿可为马，忠贤煤可为矿，大罪十五。
Zhang Shikui, a licentiate of Liangxiang, was put to death over a dispute about a coal mine, on the pretext of illegal mining. If someone stole a handful of earth from the Changling imperial tomb, how would that be punished? Zhao Gao could call a deer a horse; Zhongxian can call coal a mine—great crime fifteen.
24
王思敬等牧地细事，责在有司。 忠贤乃幽置槛阱，恣意搒掠，视士命如草菅，大罪十六。
The grazing-land disputes involving Wang Sijing and others were minor matters for which the responsible officials should have answered. Yet Zhongxian secretly imprisoned them and tortured them at will, treating scholars' lives like weeds—great crime sixteen.
25
给事中周士朴执纠织监。 忠贤竟停其升迁，使吏部不得专铨除，言官不敢司封驳，大罪十七。
Supervising Secretary Zhou Shipu investigated and corrected abuses at the Imperial Weaving Bureau. Zhongxian actually blocked his promotion, so that the Ministry of Personnel could no longer manage appointments on its own and remonstrating officials no longer dared review and reject edicts—great crime seventeen.
26
北镇抚刘侨不肯杀人媚人，忠贤以不善锻炼，遂致削籍。 示大明之律令可以不守，而忠贤之律令不敢不遵，大罪十八。
Liu Qiao of the Northern Prison Guard refused to kill men to please others; Zhongxian, claiming he was poor at extracting confessions under torture, had him removed from office. This showed that the laws of the Great Ming might be ignored, while Zhongxian's laws dared not be disobeyed—great crime eighteen.
27
给事中魏大中遵旨莅任，忽传旨诘责。 及大中回奏，台省交章，又再亵王言。 毋论玩言官于股掌，而煌煌天语，朝夕纷更，大罪十九。
Supervising Secretary Wei Dazhong took up his post by imperial order, then suddenly received an edict rebuking him. When Dazhong submitted his reply and the censorate and secretariat rallied with memorial after memorial, the emperor's words were again twice debased. To say nothing of toying with remonstrating officials at will—the august words of the throne were changed back and forth morning and evening—great crime nineteen.
28
东厂之设，原以缉奸。 自忠贤受事，日以快私仇、行倾陷为事。 纵野子傅应星、陈居恭、傅继教辈，投匦设阱。 片语稍违，驾帖立下，势必兴同文馆狱而后已，大罪二十。
The Eastern Depot was originally established to hunt down traitors. Since Zhongxian took charge, his daily work has been settling private scores and framing others. He unleashed lowborn agents such as Fu Yingxing, Chen Jugong, and Fu Jijiao to drop denunciations into the complaint box and lay traps. At the slightest dissenting phrase an arrest warrant would be issued at once; he would not stop until he had raised a persecution on the scale of the Tongwen Guan case—great crime twenty.
29
边警未息，内外戒严，东厂访缉何事？ 前奸细韩宗功潜入长安，实主忠贤司房之邸，事露始去。 假令天不悔祸，宗功事成，未知九庙生灵安顿何地，大罪二十一。
Border alarms had not yet subsided and the realm was on alert within and without—what business did the Eastern Depot have running searches? The spy Han Zonggong had earlier infiltrated the capital and was actually staying at the mansion of Zhongxian's chief steward; he did not leave until the affair came to light. Had Heaven not turned from this calamity and Han Zonggong's plot succeeded, there is no telling where the empire's altars and its people would have found refuge—great crime twenty-one.
30
祖制，不蓄内兵，原有深意。 忠贤与奸相沈纮创立内操，薮匿奸宄，安知无大盗、刺客为敌国窥伺者潜入其中。 一旦变生肘腋，可为深虑，大罪二十二。
Ancestral institutions forbade keeping palace troops, and for good reason. Zhongxian and the treacherous minister Shen Hong established inner drill troops, a nest in which to hide villains—who can say that no brigands or assassins sent by enemy states had infiltrated them? If trouble erupted close at hand it would be profoundly dangerous—great crime twenty-two.
31
忠贤进香涿州，警跸传呼，清尘垫道，人以为大驾出幸。 及其归也，改驾四马，羽幢青盖，夹护环遮，俨然乘舆矣。 其间入幕效谋，叩马献策者，实繁有徒。 忠贤此时自视为何如人哉？ 大罪二十三。
When Zhongxian went to offer incense at Zhuozhou, with imperial guards clearing the way and roads swept clean, people took it for an imperial progress. On his return he rode a four-horse carriage with feather banners and a green canopy, ringed by escorts—it looked exactly like the imperial carriage. All the while many men entered his inner circle to offer counsel and stopped his horse to present plans. What kind of man did Zhongxian take himself to be at that moment? Great crime twenty-three.
32
夫宠极则骄，恩多成怨。 闻今春忠贤走马御前，陛下射杀其马，贷以不死。 忠贤不自伏罪，进有傲色，退有怨言，朝夕堤防，介介不释。 从来乱臣贼子，只争一念，放肆遂至不可收拾，奈何养虎兕于肘腋间乎！ 此又寸脔忠贤，不足尽其辜者，大罪二十四。
When favor reaches its height, pride follows; too much kindness turns to resentment. I have heard that this spring Zhongxian galloped his horse before Your Majesty, and that Your Majesty shot and killed the horse but spared his life. Zhongxian did not humble himself; he wore arrogance when he approached you and grumbled when he withdrew, on guard morning and night and never at ease. Rebellious ministers and traitors have always turned on a single thought; their license soon becomes uncontrollable—why keep a tiger and a rhinoceros at your elbow! This too barely scratches the surface of Zhongxian's guilt—great crime twenty-four.
33
凡此逆迹，昭然在人耳目。 乃内廷畏祸而不敢言，外廷结舌而莫敢奏。 间或奸状败露，则又有奉圣夫人为之弥缝。 甚至无耻之徒，攀附枝叶，依托门墙，更相表里，迭为呼应。 积威所劫，致掖廷之中，但知有忠贤，不知有陛下； 都城之内，亦但知有忠贤，不知有陛下。 即如前日，忠贤已往涿州，一切政务必星夜驰请，待其既旋，诏旨始下。 天颜咫尺，忽慢至此，陛下之威灵尚尊于忠贤否邪？ 陛下春秋鼎盛，生杀予夺，岂不可以自主？ 何为受制幺纻小丑，令中外大小惴惴莫必其命？ 伏乞大奋雷霆，集文武勋戚，敕刑部严讯，以正国法，并出奉圣夫人于外，用消隐忧，臣死且不朽。
All these rebellious acts were plain for all to see and hear. Yet within the palace they feared retribution and dared not speak; outside, officials held their tongues and no one dared to memorialize. When evil conduct occasionally came to light, Lady Fengsheng would patch things over for him. Even shameless men clung to his branches, leaned on his faction, worked inside and outside together, and echoed one another in turn. His accumulated power so overawed the inner palace that they knew only Zhongxian and not Your Majesty; and within the capital too they knew only Zhongxian and not Your Majesty. Just the other day, while Zhongxian was away at Zhuozhou, every matter of state had to be rushed to him overnight, and no edict was issued until he had returned. Your face is within reach, yet deference has fallen to this point—is Your Majesty's authority still honored above Zhongxian's? Your Majesty is in the prime of life, with the power of life and death in your hands—can you not act on your own authority? Why be ruled by an insignificant petty scoundrel, leaving everyone within and without anxious and uncertain of their fate? I humbly beg Your Majesty to rouse the thunderbolt of imperial wrath, summon civil and military officials and meritorious kin, order the Ministry of Justice to conduct a rigorous trial and uphold the law, and remove Lady Fengsheng from the palace to dispel this hidden peril—even if I die, my name will endure.
34
忠贤初闻疏，惧甚。 其党王体乾及客氏力为保持，遂令魏广微调旨切责涟。 先是，涟疏就欲早朝面奏。 值次日免朝，恐再宿机泄，遂于会极门上之，忠贤乃得为计。 涟愈愤，拟对仗复劾之，忠贤诇知，遏帝不御朝者三日。 及帝出，群阉数百人衷甲夹陛立，敕左班官不得奏事，涟乃止。
When Zhongxian first heard the memorial, he was terrified. His allies Wang Tiqian and Lady Ke rallied to protect him, and Wei Guangwei was made to draft an edict sharply rebuking Lian. Earlier, as soon as Lian finished his memorial he had intended to present it in person at the morning audience. Court was canceled the next day; fearing another night's delay would expose his plan, he submitted it at the Gate of Supreme Harmony, and Zhongxian was then able to counter him. Lian grew still angrier and planned to remonstrate again at formal audience; Zhongxian learned of it and kept the emperor from holding court for three days. When the emperor finally appeared, several hundred eunuchs in hidden armor lined the steps; officials of the left rank were forbidden to speak, and Lian had to desist.
35
自是，忠贤日谋杀涟。 至十月，吏部尚书赵南星既逐，廷推代者，涟注籍不与。 忠贤矫旨责涟大不敬，无人臣礼，偕吏部侍郎陈于廷、佥都御史左光斗并削籍。 忠贤恨不已，再兴汪文言狱，将罗织杀涟。 五年，其党大理丞徐大化劾涟、光斗党同伐异，招权纳贿，命逮文言下狱鞫之。 许显纯严鞫文言，使引涟纳熊廷弼贿。 文言仰天大呼曰：“世岂有贪赃杨大洪哉！ ”至死不承。 大洪者，涟别字也。 显纯乃自为狱词，坐涟赃二万，遂逮涟。 士民数万人拥道攀号，所历村市，悉焚香建醮，祈祐涟生还。 比下诏狱，显纯酷法拷讯，体无完肤。 其年七月遂于夜中毙之，年五十四。
From then on Zhongxian plotted every day to murder Lian. By the tenth month, after Minister of Personnel Zhao Nanxing had been driven out, the court nominated a successor but Lian's name was left off the list. Zhongxian forged an edict rebuking Lian for gross disrespect and breach of a subject's duty, and Lian, Vice Minister of Personnel Chen Yuting, and Censor-in-chief Zuo Guangdou were all stripped of office. Zhongxian's hatred did not abate; he revived the Wang Wenyan case, intending to frame Lian and have him killed. In the fifth year his ally Xu Dahua, a grand councilor of the Court of Review, impeached Lian and Guangdou for factional collusion, monopolizing power, and taking bribes, and Wenyan was ordered arrested and interrogated in prison. Xu Xianchun rigorously interrogated Wenyan and tried to make him implicate Lian in taking bribes from Xiong Tingbi. Wenyan looked to heaven and cried out, "How could there be a corrupt Yang Dahong in the world! " He never confessed, even unto death. Dahong was Lian's courtesy name. Xianchun then fabricated the indictment himself, convicted Lian of accepting twenty thousand in bribes, and had him arrested. Tens of thousands of scholars and commoners lined the road weeping and calling out; in every village and market he passed they burned incense and held rites, praying for his safe return. Once he was sent to the imperial prison, Xianchun tortured him so brutally that not a patch of skin on his body was left whole. That year, in the seventh month, he was killed in the dead of night at the age of fifty-four.
36
涟素贫，产入官不及千金。 母妻止宿谯楼，二子至乞食以养。 征赃令急，乡人竞出赀助之，下至卖菜佣亦为输助。 其节义感人如此。 崇祯初，赠太子太保、兵部尚书，谥忠烈，官其一子。
Lian had always been poor; the property confiscated by the state did not even amount to a thousand taels. His mother and wife had nowhere to stay but the watchtower, and his two sons had to beg for food to support them. The demand for recovered bribes was urgent; villagers rushed to contribute what they could, and even vegetable peddlers and day laborers paid their share. Such was the power of his integrity and righteousness. At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously granted the titles Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, given the posthumous name Loyal and Ardent, and one son was granted office.
37
左光斗，字遗直，桐城人。 万历三十五年进士。 除中书舍人。 选授御史，巡视中城。 捕治吏部豪恶吏，获假印七十余，假官一百余人，辇下震悚。
Zuo Guangdou, courtesy name Yizhi, was a native of Tongcheng. He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-fifth year of the Wanli reign. He was appointed a central drafting attendant. He was selected and appointed censor, with responsibility for inspecting the inner city. He arrested and punished the Ministry of Personnel's most brutal clerks, seized more than seventy false seals and more than a hundred impostor officials, and the capital was shaken.
38
出理屯田，言：“北人不知水利，一年而地荒，二年而民徙，三年而地与民尽矣。 今欲使旱不为灾，涝不为害，惟有兴水利一法。 ”因条上三因十四议：曰因天之时，因地之利，因人之情； 曰议浚川，议疏渠，议引流，议设坝，议建闸，议设陂，议相地，议筑塘，议招徠，议择人，议择将，议兵屯，议力田设科，议富民拜爵。 其法犁然具备，诏悉允行。 水利大兴，北人始知艺稻。 邹元标尝曰：“三十年前，都人不知稻草何物，今所在皆稻，种水田利也。 ”阉人刘朝称东宫令旨，索戚畹废庄。 光斗不启封还之，曰：“尺土皆殿下有，今日安敢私受。 ”阉人愤而去。
Sent out to administer military colonies, he said, "Northerners know nothing of irrigation; in one year the land lies waste, in two years the people flee, and in three years both land and people are gone. If drought is not to become disaster and flooding is not to become ruin, there is only one remedy: develop irrigation. " He then submitted in detail three foundations and fourteen proposals: work with the seasons, work with the land, and work with the people; and proposals to dredge rivers, clear canals, divert water, build dams and sluices, create reservoirs, survey terrain, build embankments, recruit settlers, choose administrators and commanders, garrison troops on the land, levy taxes on reclaimed fields, and grant titles to wealthy commoners. His plan was complete in every detail, and an edict approved it in full. Irrigation was greatly expanded, and northerners learned to grow rice for the first time. Zou Yuanbiao once said, "Thirty years ago people in the capital did not even know what rice straw was; now rice is everywhere—the benefit of paddy fields. " The eunuch Liu Chao, claiming an order from the Eastern Palace, demanded an abandoned estate belonging to an imperial in-law. Guangdou returned it unopened and said, "Every inch of land belongs to the heir apparent—how dare I accept it for myself today? " The eunuch left in a rage.
39
光宗崩，李选侍据乾清宫，迫皇长子封皇后。 光斗上言：“内廷有乾清宫，犹外廷有皇极殿，惟天子御天得居之，惟皇后配天得共居之。 其他妃嫔虽以次进御，不得恒居，非但避嫌，亦以别尊卑也。 选侍既非嫡母，又非生母，俨然尊居正宫，而殿下乃退处慈庆，不得守几筵，行大礼，名分谓何？ 选侍事先皇无脱簪戒旦之德，于殿下无拊摩养育之恩，此其人，岂可以托圣躬者？ 且殿下春秋十六龄矣，内辅以忠直老成，外辅以公孤卿贰，何虑乏人，尚须乳哺而襁负之哉？ 况睿哲初开，正宜不见可欲，何必托于妇人女子之手？ 及今不早断决，将借抚养之名，行专制之实。 武氏之祸再见于今，将来有不忍言者。 ”时选侍欲专大权，廷臣笺奏，令先进乾清，然后进慈庆。 得光斗笺，大怒，将加严谴。 数遣使宣召光斗，光斗曰：“我天子法官也，非天子召不赴。 若辈何为者？ ”选侍益怒，邀熹宗至乾清议之。 熹宗不肯往，使使取其笺视之，心以为善，趣择日移宫，光斗乃免。 当是时，宫府危疑，人情危惧，光斗与杨涟协心建议，排阉奴，扶冲主，宸极获正，两人力为多。 由是朝野并称为“杨左”。
When Emperor Guangzong died, Lady Li the Attendant seized the Palace of Heavenly Purity and pressured the eldest imperial son to make her empress. Guangdou submitted a memorial saying, "Within the palace there is the Palace of Heavenly Purity, just as in the outer court there is the Hall of Supreme Harmony; only the Son of Heaven who rules under heaven may dwell there, and only the empress who shares his station may dwell there with him. Other consorts may attend him in turn but may not live there permanently—not only to avoid suspicion, but to preserve the distinction of rank. The Attendant is neither your legitimate mother nor your birth mother, yet she occupies the principal palace as though she belonged there, while Your Highness has been sent off to Ciqing and cannot keep vigil at the mourning couch or perform the great rites—what kind of order is this? The Attendant showed the late emperor none of the devotion of a faithful consort, and toward Your Highness she showed none of the care of a nurturing mother—can such a person be entrusted with the emperor's person? Moreover, Your Highness is already sixteen; within the palace you can be guided by loyal and seasoned men, and without by the highest ministers of state—why fear a lack of counselors? Must you still need to be nursed and carried in swaddling clothes? Your keen intelligence is just awakening; this is precisely the time to keep temptation from your eyes—why must you be placed in the hands of women? If this is not decided at once, she will use the name of guardianship to exercise autocratic power in fact. The calamity of Empress Wu will repeat itself in our own day, and the consequences will be too terrible to speak of. " At that time the Attendant sought to monopolize power; court officials submitted memorials urging that the heir first enter the Palace of Heavenly Purity and then move to Ciqing. When she received Guangdou's memorial she was furious and was about to punish him severely. She repeatedly sent messengers to summon Guangdou; Guangdou said, "I am a judicial officer of the emperor; unless the emperor summons me I will not go. Who are you people? " The Attendant grew still angrier and invited Emperor Xizong to the Palace of Heavenly Purity to discuss the matter. Emperor Xizong refused to go and sent a messenger to fetch and read the memorial; approving of it, he hastened to set a day for the move, and Guangdou was spared. At that time the palace and court were in peril and the people were afraid; Guangdou and Yang Lian worked together in counsel, drove out the eunuch faction, supported the young emperor, and set the throne to rights—the two men did more than anyone. From then on court and country alike spoke of them as "Yang and Zuo."
40
未几，御史贾继春上书内阁，言帝不当薄待庶母。 光斗闻之，即上言：“先帝宴驾，大臣从乾清宫奉皇上出居慈庆宫，臣等以为不宜避选侍。 故臣于初二日具《慎守典礼肃清宫禁》一疏，宫中震怒，祸几不测。 赖皇上保全，发臣疏于内阁。 初五日，阁臣具揭再催，奉旨移宫。 至初六日，皇上登极，驾还乾清。 宫禁肃然，内外宁谧。 夫皇上既当还宫，则选侍之当移，其理明白易晓。 惟是移宫以后，自宜存大体，捐小过。 若复株连蔓引，使宫闱不安，即于国体有损。 乞立诛盗宝宫奴刘逊等，而尽宽其余。 ”帝乃宣谕百官，备述选侍凌虐圣母诸状。 及召见，又言：“朕与选侍有仇。 ”继春用是得罪去。
Before long, Censor Jia Jichun wrote to the Grand Secretariat arguing that the emperor ought not treat his stepmother harshly. When Guangdou heard this he immediately submitted a memorial saying, "When the late emperor passed away, the great ministers escorted Your Majesty from the Palace of Heavenly Purity to the Palace of Ciqing; we believed it improper to yield the palace to the Attendant. Therefore on the second day I submitted a memorial entitled "Carefully Uphold the Rites and Purify the Palace Prohibitions"; the palace was furious and disaster nearly struck. Only because Your Majesty protected me was my memorial sent out to the Grand Secretariat. On the fifth day the grand secretaries submitted another note urging action, and an edict ordered the move. By the sixth day Your Majesty ascended the throne and returned to the Palace of Heavenly Purity. The palace was restored to order, and peace returned within and without. Since Your Majesty ought to return to the palace, the Attendant ought to move—the principle is plain. After the move, however, the larger interest should be preserved and small faults overlooked. If charges are extended by entangled implication and the inner quarters are unsettled, the dignity of the state itself will suffer. I beg that the palace slaves who stole treasures, Liu Xun and the others, be executed at once, while all the rest be fully pardoned. " The emperor then addressed the officials, fully recounting how the Attendant had bullied and abused the empress dowager. When he summoned them to audience he also said, "I bear a grudge against the Attendant. " Jichun was thus disgraced and dismissed.
41
时廷臣议改元。 或议削泰昌弗纪，或议去万历四十八年，即以今年为泰昌，或议以明年为泰昌，后年为天启。 光斗力排其说，请从今年八月以前为万历，以后为泰昌，议遂定。 孙如游由中旨入阁，抗疏请斥之。 出督畿辅学政，力杜请寄，识鉴如神。
At that time court officials debated changing the reign title. Some proposed omitting the Taichang reign altogether; some proposed dropping the forty-eighth year of Wanli and making the current year Taichang; others proposed making the next year Taichang and the year after Tianqi. Guangdou forcefully rejected these proposals and argued that everything before the eighth month of the current year should count as Wanli and everything after as Taichang; the debate was then settled. When Sun Ruyou entered the Grand Secretariat by secret edict, Guangdou submitted a bold memorial demanding his dismissal. Sent out to supervise education in the capital region, he firmly shut down backdoor requests; his judgment was uncanny.
42
天启初，廷议起用熊廷弼，罪言官魏应嘉等。 光斗独抗疏争之，言廷弼才优而量不宏，昔以守辽则有余，今以复辽则不足。 已而廷弼竟败。 三年秋，疏请召还文震孟、满朝荐、毛士龙、徐大相等，并乞召继春及范济世。 济世亦论“移宫”事与光斗异者，疏上不纳。 其年擢大理丞，进少卿。
Early in the Tianqi reign, the court debated reappointing Xiong Tingbi and punishing remonstrating officials such as Wei Yingjia. Guangdou alone submitted a bold memorial in dissent, arguing that Xiong Tingbi's talent was superior but his breadth of vision was limited: he had more than enough to hold Liaodong, but not enough to recover it. Before long Xiong Tingbi was indeed defeated. That autumn in the third year he submitted a memorial asking that Wen Zhenmeng, Man Chaojian, Mao Shilong, Xu Dahuang, and others be recalled, and also begged that Jichun and Fan Jishi be summoned back. Jishi also took a view of the Transfer of the Palace affair different from Guangdou's; the memorial was not accepted. That year he was promoted to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and then to vice minister.
43
明年二月拜左佥都御史。 是时，韩爌、赵南星、高攀龙、杨涟、郑三俊、李邦华、魏大中诸人咸居要地，光斗与相得，务为危言核论，甄别流品，正人咸赖之，而忌者浸不能容。 光斗与给事中阮大铖同里，招之入京，会吏科都给事中缺，当迁者，首周士朴，次大铖，次大中。 大铖邀中旨，勒士朴不迁，以为己地。 赵南星恶之，欲例转大铖，大铖疑光斗发其谋，恨甚。 熊明遇、徐良彦皆欲得佥都御史，而南星引光斗为之，两人亦恨光斗。 江西人又以他故衔大中，遂共嗾给事中傅櫆劾光斗、大中与汪文言比而为奸。 光斗疏辨，且诋櫆结东厂理刑傅继教为昆弟。 櫆恚，再疏讦光斗。 光斗乞罢，事得解。
In the second month of the following year he was appointed Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief. At this time Han Kuang, Zhao Nanxing, Gao Panlong, Yang Lian, Zheng Sanjun, Li Banghua, Wei Dazhong, and others all held key posts. Guangdou worked well with them, issuing stern warnings and exacting judgments, sorting men by character. Upright officials relied on them, while their enemies grew ever less able to tolerate them. Guangdou and Supervising Secretary Ruan Dacheng were from the same home district, and he invited Dacheng to the capital. When the post of supervising secretary in the Department of Personnel fell vacant, the order of promotion should have been Zhou Shipu first, then Dacheng, then Dazhong. Dacheng obtained a secret edict and pressured Shipu not to be promoted, clearing the way for himself. Zhao Nanxing disliked him and wanted to transfer Dacheng by routine precedent. Dacheng suspected Guangdou had exposed his scheme and hated him bitterly. Xiong Mingyu and Xu Liangyan both wanted the post of assistant censor-in-chief, but Nanxing installed Guangdou instead, and the two men resented Guangdou as well. Jiangxi officials also bore a grudge against Dazhong for other reasons. Together they instigated Supervising Secretary Fu Kui to impeach Guangdou and Dazhong for consorting with Wang Wuyan and engaging in villainy. Guangdou submitted a memorial in his defense and also denounced Kui for treating Fu Jijiao, the Eastern Depot's judicial officer, as a sworn brother. Kui was enraged and submitted another memorial attacking Guangdou. Guangdou asked to be dismissed, and the matter was dropped.
44
杨涟劾魏忠贤，光斗与其谋，又与攀龙共发崔呈秀赃私，忠贤暨其党咸怒。 及忠贤逐南星、攀龙、大中，次将及涟、光斗。 光斗愤甚，草奏劾忠贤及魏广微三十二斩罪，拟十一月二日上之，先遣妻子南还。 忠贤诇知，先二日假会推事与涟俱削籍。 群小恨不已，复构文言狱，入光斗名，遣使往逮。 父老子弟拥马首号哭，声震原野，缇骑亦为雪涕。 至则下诏狱酷讯。 许显纯诬以受杨镐、熊廷弼贿，涟等初不承，已而恐以不承为酷刑所毙，冀下法司，得少缓死为后图。 诸人俱自诬服，光斗坐赃二万。 忠贤乃矫旨，仍令显纯五日一追比，不下法司，诸人始悔失计。 容城孙奇逢者，节侠士也，与定兴鹿正以光斗有德于畿辅，倡议醵金，诸生争应之。 得金数千，谋代输，缓其狱，而光斗与涟已同日为狱卒所毙，时五年七月二十有六日也，年五十一。
When Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian, Guangdou joined the effort and, together with Panlong, exposed Cui Chengxiu's corruption. Zhongxian and his faction were furious. After Zhongxian drove out Nanxing, Panlong, and Dazhong, Lian and Guangdou were next. Guangdou was furious. He drafted a memorial impeaching Zhongxian and Wei Guangwei on thirty-two capital offenses, planning to submit it on the second day of the eleventh month, and first sent his wife and children home to the south. Zhongxian learned of this through spies. Two days early, on the pretext of a joint recommendation, he and Lian were both stripped of office. The petty faction's hatred did not end. They fabricated the Wuyan case again, added Guangdou's name, and sent agents to arrest him. Old men and young blocked his horse, weeping and wailing until the sound shook the open country. Even the imperial riders wept. On arrival he was sent to the imperial prison for brutal interrogation. Xu Xianchun falsely charged them with taking bribes from Yang Hao and Xiong Tingbi. At first Lian and the others refused to confess, but then they feared death under torture. They hoped that if the case went to the regular courts they might gain a little time and plan for later. All of them falsely confessed. Guangdou was convicted of embezzling twenty thousand taels. Zhongxian then forged an edict ordering Xianchun to continue torture sessions every five days without sending the case to the regular courts. Only then did the men regret their mistake. Sun Qifeng of Rongcheng was a man of integrity and chivalry. Together with Lu Zheng of Dingxing, believing Guangdou had done good for the capital region, he proposed a public collection of funds, and students rushed to contribute. They raised several thousand taels and planned to pay on his behalf to ease the case, but Guangdou and Lian had already been killed the same day by prison guards. It was the twenty-sixth day of the seventh month of the fifth year; he was fifty-one.
45
光斗既死，赃犹未竟。 忠贤令抚按严追，系其群从十四人。 长兄光霁坐累死，母以哭子死。 都御史周应秋犹以所司承追不力，疏趣之，由是诸人家族尽破。 及忠贤定《三朝要典》，“移宫”一案以涟、光斗为罪魁，议开棺僇尸。 有解之者，乃免。 忠贤既诛，赠光斗右都御史，录其一子。 已，再赠太子少保。 福王时，追谥忠毅。
Even after Guangdou's death, the embezzlement charge was still pursued. Zhongxian ordered the provincial officials to pursue payment ruthlessly and imprisoned fourteen of his clansmen. His elder brother Guangji died from exhaustion in custody, and his mother died from grief for her son. Censor-in-Chief Zhou Yingqiu still rebuked the responsible offices for lax collection and submitted a memorial pressing them on. From this all their families were ruined. When Zhongxian finalized the Essential Records of Three Reigns, the Transfer of the Palace case treated Lian and Guangdou as chief culprits, and there was talk of opening their coffins to desecrate their corpses. Someone interceded, and the proposal was dropped. After Zhongxian was executed, Guangdou was posthumously made Right Censor-in-Chief and one son was granted office. Later he was again posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent. Under the Prince of Fu, he was posthumously given the temple name Loyal and Resolute.
46
弟光先，由乡举官御史，巡按浙江。 任满，既出境，许都反东阳。 光先闻变疾返，讨平之。 福王既立，马士英荐阮大铖，光先争不可。 后大铖得志，逮光先。 乱亟道阻，光先间行走徽岭。 缇骑索不得，乃止。
His younger brother Guangxian, a provincial graduate, served as censor and conducted an inspection tour of Zhejiang. When his term ended and he had already left the province, Xu Du rebelled at Dongyang. Guangxian heard of the revolt and rushed back, suppressing and pacifying it. After the Prince of Fu was enthroned, Ma Shiying recommended Ruan Dacheng. Guangxian argued strenuously against it. Later, once Dacheng got his way, he had Guangxian arrested. With chaos spreading and the roads blocked, Guangxian made his way by back roads through the Huiling pass. The imperial riders could not find him and gave up the pursuit.
47
魏大中，字孔时，嘉善人。 自为诸生，读书砥行，从高攀龙受业。 家酷贫，意豁如也。 举于乡，家人易新衣冠，怒而毁之。 第万历四十四年进士，官行人。 数奉使，秋毫无所扰。
Wei Dazhong, whose style name was Kongshi, came from Jiashan. From his days as a student he devoted himself to study and moral discipline, studying under Gao Panlong. His family was desperately poor, yet his spirit remained open and untroubled. When he passed the provincial examination, his family put on new clothes and caps; he angrily tore them off. He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fourth year of Wanli and served as Bearer of Edicts. Sent on mission after mission, he never took so much as a hair's worth from those he visited.
48
天启元年，擢工科给事中。 杨镐、李如桢既论大辟，以佥都御史王德完言，大学士韩爌遽拟旨减死。 大中愤，抗疏力争，诋德完晚节不振，尽丧典型，语并侵爌。 帝为诘责大中，而德完恚甚，言曩不举李三才为大中所怒。 两人互诋讦，疏屡上，爌亦引咎辞位。 御史周宗建、徐扬先、张捷、徐景濂、温皋谟，给事中硃钦相右德完，交章论大中，久而后定。
In the first year of Tianqi he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Department of Works. After Yang Hao and Li Ruzhen had been sentenced to death, Grand Secretary Han Kuang, on the word of Assistant Censor-in-Chief Wang Dewan, hastily drafted an edict commuting the sentence. Dazhong was indignant. He submitted a bold memorial arguing forcefully, denouncing Dewan for failing in his later years and abandoning every standard of integrity, and his words also impugned Han Kuang. The emperor reprimanded Dazhong, while Dewan was furious, saying that Dazhong had long been angry with him for failing to recommend Li Sanicai. The two men traded denunciations in memorial after memorial, and Han Kuang also accepted blame and resigned. Censors Zhou Zongjian, Xu Yangxian, Zhang Jie, Xu Jinglian, and Wen Gaomo, and Supervising Secretary Zhu Qinxiang sided with Dewan and submitted successive memorials attacking Dazhong. Only after a long dispute was the matter settled.
49
明年偕同官周朝瑞等两疏劾大学士沈纮，语侵魏进忠、客氏。 及议“红丸”事，力请诛方从哲、崔文升、李可灼，且追论郑国泰倾害东宫罪。 持议峻切，大为邪党所仄目。 太常少卿王绍徽素与东林为难，营求巡抚，大中恶其人，特疏请斥绍徽，绍徽卒自引去。 再迁礼科左给事中。 是时恤典冒滥，每大臣卒，其子弟夤缘要路以请，无不如志。 大中素疾之，一切裁以典制。
The following year, together with colleagues including Zhou Chaorui, he twice submitted memorials impeaching Grand Secretary Shen Hong, with language that also impugned Wei Jinzhong and Ke Shi. When the Red Pill affair was debated, he forcefully called for the execution of Fang Congzhe, Cui Wensheng, and Li Kezhuo, and also pursued charges against Zheng Guotai for harming the crown prince. His positions were stern and uncompromising, and the evil faction watched him with bitter resentment. Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Wang Shaohui had long been at odds with the Donglin faction. Seeking a provincial governorship, he earned Dazhong's dislike, and Dazhong specially submitted a memorial asking that Shaohui be dismissed. Shaohui ultimately withdrew on his own. He was transferred again to left supervising secretary in the Department of Rites. At that time condolence honors were handed out with reckless extravagance. Whenever a great minister died, his sons and younger brothers used connections at key posts to request favors, and almost always got what they wanted. Dazhong had long resented this and cut every request down to what statute allowed.
50
四年迁吏科都给事中。 大中居官不以家自随，二苍头给爨而已，入朝则键其户，寂无一人。 有外吏以苞苴至，举发之，自是无敢及大中门者。 吏部尚书赵南星知其贤，事多咨访。 朝士不能得南星意，率怨大中。 而是时牴排东林者多屏废，方恨南星辈次骨。 东林中，又各以地分左右。 大中尝驳苏松巡抚王象恒恤典，山东人居言路者咸怒。 及驳浙江巡抚刘一焜，江西人亦大怒。 给事中章允儒，江西人也，性尤忮，嗾其同官傅櫆假汪文言发难。
In the fourth year he was made supervising secretary in the Department of Personnel. Dazhong did not bring his family to the capital—only two servants to cook for him. When he went to court he locked his door, and the house stood empty and silent. When an outside official brought a bribe, he exposed it. After that no one dared approach his door. Minister of Personnel Zhao Nanxing recognized his worth and often consulted him. Court officials who could not win Nanxing's favor generally blamed Dazhong. Meanwhile many who had opposed the Donglin faction had been dismissed and sidelined, and they hated Nanxing and his allies to the bone. Within the Donglin faction itself, men again split into regional camps. Dazhong once rejected the condolence honors for Sufu Governor Wang Xiangheng, angering Shandong officials on the remonstrance circuit. When he also rejected the honors for Zhejiang Governor Liu Yikun, Jiangxi officials were furious as well. Supervising Secretary Zhang Yunru, a Jiangxi man with an especially vicious temperament, instigated his colleague Fu Kui to launch an attack using Wang Wuyan as pretext.
51
文言者，歙人。 初为县吏，智巧任术，负侠气。 于玉立遣入京刺事，输赀为监生，用计破齐、楚、浙三党。 察东宫伴读王安贤而知书，倾心结纳，与谈当世流品。 光、熹之际，外廷倚刘一燝，而安居中以次行诸善政，文言交关力为多。 魏忠贤既杀安，府丞邵辅忠遂劾文言，褫其监生。 既出都，复逮下吏，得末减。 益游公卿间，舆马尝填溢户外。 大学士叶向高用为内阁中书，大中及韩爌、赵南星、杨涟、左光斗与往来，颇有迹。
Wuyan was a man of She county. At first he was a county clerk—clever, scheming, and full of chivalrous daring. Yu Yuli sent him to the capital to gather intelligence. He paid his way into the Imperial College and by stratagem broke the Qi, Chu, and Zhe factions. Seeing that Eastern Palace companion reader Wang An was worthy and well read, he wholeheartedly befriended him and talked with him about the character of men of the age. Between the reigns of Guangzong and Xizong, the outer court relied on Liu Yijiao while good policies in the inner quarters were carried out through Wang An—and Wuyan's connections did much of the work. After Wei Zhongxian killed Wang An, Assistant Prefect Shao Fuzhong impeached Wuyan and stripped him of his student status. After leaving the capital he was arrested again and sent before the magistrates, receiving a reduced sentence. He moved ever more freely among high officials; carriages and horses often filled the street outside his door. Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao employed him as a Grand Secretariat copyist. Dazhong, Han Kuang, Zhao Nanxing, Yang Lian, and Zuo Guangdou all had dealings with him, and clear traces remained.
52
会给事中阮大铖与光斗、大中有隙，遂与允儒定计，嘱櫆劾文言，并劾大中貌陋心险，色取行违，与光斗等交通文言，肆为奸利。 疏入，忠贤大喜，立下文言诏狱。 大中时方迁吏科，上疏力辩，诏许履任。 御史袁化中、给事中甄淑等相继为大中、光斗辨。 大学士叶向高以举用文言，亦引罪求罢。 狱方急，御史黄尊素语镇抚刘侨曰：“文言无足惜，不可使搢绅祸由此起。 ”侨颔之，狱辞无所连。 文言廷杖褫职，牵及者获免。 大中乃遵旨履任。 明日，鸿胪报名面恩，忠贤忽矫旨责大中互讦未竣，不得赴新任。 故事，鸿胪报名状无批谕旨者，举朝骇愕。 櫆亦言中旨不宜旁出，大中乃复视事。
Supervising Secretary Ruan Dacheng happened to be at odds with Guangdou and Dazhong. He joined Yunru in a plan, instructing Kui to impeach Wuyan and also to impeach Dazhong as ugly in face and treacherous at heart, outwardly upright but inwardly corrupt, consorting with Guangdou and others through Wuyan to seek illicit profit. When the memorial arrived, Zhongxian was delighted and immediately sent Wuyan to the imperial prison. Dazhong had just been transferred to the Department of Personnel. He submitted a forceful memorial in his defense, and an edict allowed him to take up his post. Censor Yuan Huazhong, Supervising Secretary Zhen Shu, and others successively spoke up for Dazhong and Guangdou. Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao, for having employed Wuyan, also accepted blame and asked to resign. The case was urgent. Censor Huang Zunsu said to Grand Coordinator Liu Qiao: "Wuyan is not worth sparing, but we must not let a calamity for the gentry begin here. " Liu Qiao nodded. The case testimony implicated no one else. Wuyan was flogged at court and stripped of office, and those implicated were spared. Dazhong then obeyed the edict and took up his post. The next day, when the Court of State Ceremonial registered names for the audience of grace, Zhongxian suddenly forged an edict rebuking Dazhong on the grounds that the mutual denunciations were not yet settled and he could not take up his new post. By precedent the Court of State Ceremonial's name roll carried no edict of rebuke or approval. The whole court was shocked. Kui also argued that secret edicts ought not be issued on the side, and Dazhong then resumed his duties.
53
未几，杨涟疏劾忠贤，大中亦率同官上言：“从古君侧之奸，非遂能祸人国也。 有忠臣不惜其身以告之君，而其君不悟，乃至于不可救。 今忠贤擅威福，结党与，首杀王安以树威于内，继逐刘一燝、周嘉谟、王纪以树威于外，近且毙三戚畹家人以树威于三宫。 深结保姆客氏，伺陛下起居； 广布傅应星、陈居恭、傅继教辈，通朝中声息。 人怨于下，天怒于上，故涟不惜粉身碎首为陛下陈。 今忠贤种种罪状，陛下悉引为亲裁，代之任咎。 恐忠贤所以得温旨，即出忠贤手，而涟之疏，陛下且未及省览也。 陛下贵为天子，致三宫列嫔尽寄性命于忠贤、客氏，能不寒心？ 陛下谓宫禁严密，外廷安知，枚乘有言‘欲人弗知，莫若弗为’，未有为其事而他人不知者。 又谓左右屏而圣躬将孤立。 夫陛下一身，大小臣工所拥卫，何藉于忠贤？ 若忠贤、客氏一日不去，恐禁廷左右悉忠贤、客氏之人，非陛下之人，陛下真孤立于上耳。 ”忠贤得疏大怒，矫旨切让，尚未有以罪也。 大学士魏广微结纳忠贤，表里为奸，大中每欲纠之。 会孟冬时享，广微偃蹇后至，大中遂抗疏劾之。 广微愠，益与忠贤合。 忠贤势益张，以廷臣交攻，阳示敛戢，且曲从诸所奏请，而阴伺其隙。 迨吏部推谢应祥巡抚山西，广微遂嗾所亲陈九畴劾大中出应祥门，推举不公，贬三秩，出之外，尽逐诸正人吏部尚书赵南星等，天下大权一归于忠贤。
Before long Yang Lian submitted a memorial impeaching Zhongxian. Dazhong also led his colleagues in submitting a statement: "Since antiquity, villains beside the throne have not been able straightaway to ruin a state. There are loyal ministers who risk themselves to warn their ruler, yet when the ruler does not understand, the realm reaches the point of no salvation. Now Zhongxian monopolizes power and favor, builds factions, first killed Wang An to establish terror within, then drove out Liu Yijiao, Zhou Jiamo, and Wang Ji to establish terror without, and recently even killed retainers of three imperial consorts' households to establish terror in the three palaces. He is deeply tied to the nurse Ke Shi, watching Your Majesty's every move; He spread agents such as Fu Yingxing, Chen Jugong, and Fu Jijiao throughout the capital to carry word of everything happening at court. The people resent below and Heaven is angry above—so Lian does not spare even his life in laying this before Your Majesty. Now for every charge against Zhongxian, Your Majesty treats each as a matter you personally judged and takes the blame upon yourself in his place. I fear the gracious edicts Zhongxian enjoys come from Zhongxian's own hand, while Your Majesty has not yet even had time to read Lian's memorial. Your Majesty, exalted as Son of Heaven, have made the three palaces and every consort entrust their lives to Zhongxian and Ke Shi—can that not chill your heart? Your Majesty says the inner palace is tightly guarded and the outer court cannot know; yet Meicheng said, 'If you wish others not to know, best not do it'—no one has ever done a thing without others finding out. You also say that if your attendants are cleared away, the sacred person will stand alone. Your Majesty's person is guarded by ministers great and small—what need have you of Zhongxian? If Zhongxian and Ke Shi are not removed even for a day, I fear everyone at your side in the forbidden precincts will be Zhongxian's and Ke Shi's people, not yours—and Your Majesty will truly stand alone on high. " Zhongxian received the memorial and flew into a rage; he forged an edict sharply rebuking them, but as yet had no crime with which to punish them. Grand Secretary Wei Guangwei had allied with Zhongxian and conspired with him inside and out; Dazhong often wished to impeach him. At the winter solstice seasonal offering, Guangwei arrived late in arrogant defiance; Dazhong then submitted a bold memorial impeaching him. Guangwei was angry and drew even closer to Zhongxian. Zhongxian's power grew still greater; as court officials attacked him together, he outwardly showed restraint and even yielded to their various requests, while secretly watching for an opening. When the Ministry of Personnel nominated Xie Yingxiang as grand coordinator of Shanxi, Guangwei incited his intimate Chen Jiuchou to impeach Dazhong as a protégé of Yingxiang and charge unfair nomination. Dazhong was demoted three ranks and sent outside; upright men including Minister of Personnel Zhao Nanxing were all driven out, and the empire's great power passed entirely to Zhongxian.
54
明年，逆党梁梦环复劾文言，再下诏狱。 镇抚许显纯自削牍以上，南星、涟、光斗、大中及李若星、毛士龙、袁化中、缪昌期、邹维琏、邓渼、卢化鰲、钱士晋、夏之令、王之寀、徐良彦、熊明遇、周朝瑞、黄龙光、顾大章、李三才、惠世扬、施天德、黄正宾辈，无所不牵引，而以涟、光斗、大中、化中、朝瑞、大章为受杨镐、熊廷弼贿，大中坐三千，矫旨俱逮下诏狱。 乡人闻大中逮去，号泣送者数千人。 比入镇抚司，显纯酷刑拷讯，血肉狼籍。 其年七月，狱卒受指，与涟、光斗同夕毙之，故迟数日始报。 大中尸溃败，至不可识。 庄烈帝嗣位，忠贤被诛，广微、櫆、九畴、梦环并丽逆案。 大中赠太常卿，谥忠节，录其一子。
The next year, Liang Menghuan of the rebel faction again impeached Wuyan, and Wuyan was once more sent to the imperial prison. Grand Coordinator Xu Xianchun submitted a trimmed dossier upward. Nanxing, Lian, Guangdou, Dazhong, Li Ruoxing, Mao Shilong, Yuan Huazhong, Miu Changqi, Zou Weilian, Deng Mei, Lu Huao, Qian Shijin, Xia Zhiling, Wang Zhicai, Xu Liangyan, Xiong Mingyu, Zhou Chaorui, Huang Longguang, Gu Dazhang, Li Sancai, Hui Shiyang, Shi Tiande, Huang Zhengbin, and their like—none escaped implication. Lian, Guangdou, Dazhong, Huazhong, Chaorui, and Dazhang were charged with taking bribes from Yang Gao and Xiong Tingbi; Dazhong was held liable for three thousand taels. By forged edict all were seized and sent to the imperial prison. When people from his home district heard Dazhong had been seized and taken away, several thousand wept and saw him off. Once he entered the Brocade Guard office, Xianchun tortured him under brutal interrogation until flesh and blood lay scattered. That seventh month, the prison guards, acting on orders, killed him the same evening as Lian and Guangdou; report was therefore delayed several days. Dazhong's corpse had putrefied beyond recognition. When the Chongzhen Emperor succeeded, Zhongxian was executed; Guangwei, Kui, Jiuchou, and Menghuan were all entered in the treason register. Dazhong was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, given the posthumous title Loyal and Incorrupt, and one son was granted office.
55
长子学洢，字子敬。 为诸生，好学工文，有至性。 大中被逮，学洢号恸欲随行。 大中曰：“父子俱碎，无为也。 ”乃微服间行，刺探起居。 既抵都，逻卒四布，变姓名匿旅舍，昼伏夜出，称贷以完父赃。 赃未竟，而大中毙，学洢恸几绝。 扶榇归，晨夕号泣，遂病。 家人以浆进，辄麾去，曰：“诏狱中，谁半夜进一浆者？ ”竟号泣死。 崇祯初，有司以状闻，诏旌为孝子。
His eldest son was Xueyi, style name Zijing. A student, he loved learning, wrote well, and had exceptional filial devotion. When Dazhong was seized, Xueyi wailed in grief and wanted to go with him. Dazhong said, "If father and son are both destroyed, what good will it do? " Then in disguise he made his way by hidden routes to learn how his father was faring. Once he reached the capital, patrols were everywhere. He changed his name, hid in an inn, lay low by day and went out by night, and borrowed money to pay off his father's alleged bribes. Before the bribes were fully paid off, Dazhong died; Xueyi grieved until he nearly died himself. He escorted the coffin home, weeping morning and evening, and fell ill. When his family brought him broth, he always waved it away, saying, "In the imperial prison, who ever brought a cup of broth in the middle of the night? " In the end he wept himself to death. At the start of the Chongzhen reign, the local authorities reported the facts, and an edict honored him as a filial son.
56
次子学濂，有盛名。 举崇祯十六年进士。 擢庶吉士。 明年，李自成逼京师，与同官吴尔壎慷慨有所论建，大学士范景文以闻。 庄烈帝特召见两人，将任用之。 无何，京师陷，不能死，受贼户部司务职，颓其家声。 既而自惭，赋绝命词二章，缢死。 去帝殉社稷时四十日矣。
The second son, Xuelian, had great renown. He passed the jinshi examination in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen. He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor. The next year, as Li Zicheng pressed on the capital, he and his colleague Wu Erxun spoke boldly with proposals; Grand Secretary Fan Jingwen reported this to the throne. The Chongzhen Emperor specially summoned the two men, intending to employ them. Before long the capital fell. He failed to die with honor and accepted from the rebels the post of clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, disgracing his family's name. Afterward, ashamed, he composed two farewell poems and hanged himself. This was forty days after the emperor had died for the altars of soil and grain.
57
文言之再下诏狱也，显纯迫令引涟等。 文言备受五毒，不承，显纯乃手作文言供状。 文言垂死，张目大呼曰：“尔莫妄书，异时吾当与面质。 ”显纯遂即日毙之。 涟、大中等逮至，无可质者，赃悬坐而已。 诸所诬赵南星、缪昌期辈，亦并令抚按追赃。 衣冠之祸，由此遍天下。 始熊廷弼论死久，帝以孙承宗请，有诏待以不死。 刑部尚书乔允升等遂欲因朝审宽其罪，大中力持不可。 及忠贤杀大中，乃坐以纳廷弼贿云。
When Wuyan was again sent to the imperial prison, Xianchun forced him to implicate Lian and the others. Wuyan endured the full five tortures yet would not confess; Xianchun then personally wrote Wuyan's confession. Near death, Wuyan opened his eyes and shouted, "Do not write falsely—I shall confront you face to face in the time to come. " Xianchun thereupon killed him that very day. When Lian, Dazhong, and the others were seized and brought in, there was no one left to confront; the bribery charges rested on presumption alone. Those implicated, such as Zhao Nanxing and Miu Changqi, were also ordered by grand coordinators and regional inspectors to pursue recovery of alleged bribes. From this the calamity for the gentry spread throughout the empire. At first Xiong Tingbi had long been sentenced to death; on Sun Chengzong's petition the emperor issued an edict that he should be spared execution. Minister of Justice Qiao Yunsheng and others then wished to use the court review to lighten his sentence; Dazhong forcefully insisted this could not be done. When Zhongxian killed Dazhong, he was then charged with having taken bribes from Tingbi.
58
周朝瑞，字思永，临清人。 万历三十五年进士。 授中书舍人。
Zhou Chaorui, whose style name was Siyong, came from Linqing. He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-fifth year of the Wanli reign. He was appointed a drafter in the Secretariat.
59
光宗嗣位，擢吏科给事中，疏请收录先朝遗直。 俄陈慎初三要，曰信仁贤，广德泽，远邪佞。 因请留上供金花银，以佐军兴。 词多斥中贵。 中贵皆恶之，激帝怒，贬秩调外，时列谏垣甫四日也。 未出都而熹宗立，诏复故官。 疏请容纳直言，又陈考选诸弊。 日讲将举，进君臣交警之规。 帝并褒纳。 贾继春之请安李选侍也，朝瑞力驳之，与继春往复者数四。
When Emperor Guangzong succeeded, he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Personnel Bureau and memorialized requesting the recall of upright men left over from the previous reign. Soon he presented three essentials for a careful beginning: trust the benevolent and worthy, extend virtue and grace, and keep far from wicked flatterers. He therefore requested that the tribute of gold-flower silver be retained to assist military mobilization. His language heavily denounced the palace eunuchs. The eunuchs all hated him; they stirred the emperor's anger, and he was demoted and transferred outside—only four days after he had joined the remonstrance corps. Before he had left the capital, the Xizong Emperor ascended the throne, and an edict restored his former office. He memorialized asking the throne to accept blunt speech and again set forth the abuses in examination and selection. As daily lectures were about to begin, he presented admonitions on the mutual vigilance owed between ruler and minister. The emperor praised and accepted both. When Jia Jichun petitioned to reassure Lady Li the attendant consort, Chaorui forcefully rebutted him; he and Jichun exchanged memorials four times.
60
天启元年再迁礼科左给事中。 时辽事方棘，朝瑞请于阁臣中推通晓兵事者二人专司其事，而以职方郎一人专理机宜，给事中二人专主封驳，帝可之。 雄县知县王纳谏为阉人所诬，中旨镌秩。 给事中毛士龙以纠驳阉人，为府丞邵辅忠所陷，中旨除名。 朝瑞并抗疏论列。 十二月辛巳，日上有一物覆压，忽大风扬沙，天尽赤，都人骇愕，所司不以闻。 朝瑞请帝修省，而严敕内外臣工，毋斗争误国，更诘责所司不奏报之罪，帝纳之。 时帝践祚岁余，未尝亲政，权多旁落，朝瑞请帝躬览万机。 帝降旨，言政委阁臣，祖宗旧制不可紊，然其时政权故不在阁也。
In the first year of Tianqi he was again transferred to Left Supervising Secretary in the Rites Bureau. At that time the Liaodong crisis was acute. Chaorui requested that two men versed in military affairs be chosen from among the grand secretaries to manage it exclusively, with one bureau director of the Ministry of War devoted to urgent business and two supervising secretaries devoted to memorial review and rejection; the emperor approved. Wang Najian, magistrate of Xiong County, was slandered by eunuchs and demoted by secret edict. Supervising Secretary Mao Shilong, for impeaching eunuchs, was trapped by Assistant Director Shao Fuzhong and struck from the rolls by secret edict. Chaorui submitted bold memorials arguing both cases together. On the xinsi day of the twelfth month, something in the sky seemed to press down from above; suddenly a great wind blew sand, the sky turned wholly red, and the people of the capital were shocked—but the responsible offices did not report it. Chaorui asked the emperor to examine himself and reform, sternly ordered inner and outer officials not to fight one another and ruin the state, and further demanded accountability for the offices' failure to report; the emperor accepted. The emperor had been on the throne more than a year and had never personally governed; power largely lay elsewhere. Chaorui asked the emperor to attend to the myriad affairs of state himself. The emperor issued an edict saying governmental affairs were entrusted to the grand secretaries and the ancestral institutions must not be disturbed—yet at that time governmental power in fact lay not with the Grand Secretariat.
61
明年二月，广宁失，诏停经筵日讲。 朝瑞等上言：“此果出圣意，辅臣当引义争。 如辅臣阿中涓意，则其过滋大。 且主上冲龄，志意未定，独赖朝讲不辍，诸臣得一觐天颜，共白指鹿之奸。 今常朝已渐传免，倘并讲筵废之，九阍既隔，无谒见时，司马门之报格不入，吕大防之贬不及知，国家大事去矣。 ”会礼部亦以为言，乃命日讲如故。
The next second month, Guangning was lost; an edict halted the classics lecture and daily audience. Chaorui and others submitted: "If this truly comes from the sacred will, the assisting ministers ought to argue by principle against it. If the assisting ministers cater to the eunuchs' wishes, the offense grows all the greater. Moreover the sovereign is young and his intentions are unsettled; he relies alone on uninterrupted court lectures so that officials may behold the imperial countenance and together expose the deer-for-horse deceit. Regular audiences are already often waived; if the lecture hall is also abandoned, the nine gates will stand between us with no time of audience, reports from the Sima Gate will be blocked from entry, and demotions like Lu Dafang's will reach the emperor too late to know—the great affairs of state will be lost. " The Ministry of Rites also spoke likewise, and the daily lecture was ordered to continue as before.
62
已，偕诸给事御史惠世扬、左光斗等极论大学士沈纮结中官练兵，为肘腋之贼。 纮疏辨。 朝瑞等尽发其贿交魏进忠、卢受、刘朝、客氏，而末复侵其私人邵辅忠、徐大化。 语过激，夺疏首世扬俸。 大化尝承要人指，力攻熊廷弼，朝瑞恶之。 无何，王化贞弃广宁逃，大化又请立诛廷弼。 朝瑞以廷弼才可用，请令带罪守山海，疏四上，并抑不行。 大化遂力诋朝瑞，朝瑞愤，亦丑诋大化，所司为两解之。 朝瑞方擢太仆少卿，而大化为魏忠贤腹心，必欲杀朝瑞，窜其名汪文言狱中，与杨涟等五人并逮下镇抚狱，坐妄议“移宫”及受廷弼贿万金。 五日再讯，搒掠备至，竟毙之狱。 崇祯初，赠大理卿，予一子官。 福王时，谥忠毅。
Later, together with supervising secretaries and censors Hui Shiyang, Zuo Guangdou, and others, he forcefully denounced Grand Secretary Shen Hong for allying with eunuchs to drill troops—a villain at the emperor's armpit. Hong submitted a memorial in his defense. Chaorui and the others fully disclosed his bribery ties with Wei Jinzhong, Lu Shou, Liu Chao, and Ke Shi, and at the end again attacked his private associates Shao Fuzhong and Xu Dahua. The language was excessively sharp; the lead memorialist Shiyang's salary was suspended. Dahua had once acted on a powerful man's orders and fiercely attacked Xiong Tingbi; Chaorui detested him. Before long Wang Huazhen abandoned Guangning and fled; Dahua again requested immediate execution of Tingbi. Chaorui held that Tingbi's talent could still be used and requested that he be allowed to hold Shanhai Pass while still under sentence; he submitted four memorials, all suppressed and not acted on. Dahua then fiercely slandered Chaorui; Chaorui, enraged, also vilified Dahua; the responsible office mediated between the two. Chaorui had just been promoted Junior Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud, while Dahua, as Wei Zhongxian's trusted inner man, was determined to kill Chaorui. He inserted Chaorui's name into Wuyan's prison case, and together with Yang Lian and four others Chaorui was seized and sent to the Brocade Guard prison, charged with reckless discussion of the "move-palace" affair and taking ten thousand taels in bribes from Tingbi. After five days he was interrogated again; beating and torture were applied to the full, and in the end he died in prison. At the start of the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously made Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, and one son was granted office. Under the Prince of Fu he was given the posthumous title Loyal and Resolute.
63
袁化中，字民谐，武定人。 万历三十五年进士。 历知内黄、泾阳，有善政。
Yuan Huazhong, whose style name was Minhe, came from Wuding. He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-fifth year of the Wanli reign. He successively served as magistrate of Neihuang and Jingyang, with benevolent administration.
64
泰昌元年擢御史。 时熹宗冲龄践阼，上无母后，宫府危疑。 化中上疏劾辅臣方从哲，报闻。 天启元年二月，疏陈时事可忧者八：曰宫禁渐弛，曰言路渐轻，曰法纪渐替，曰贿赂渐章，曰边疆渐坏，曰职掌渐失，曰宦官渐盛，曰人心渐离。 语皆剀切。 出按宣、大，以忧归。 服除，起掌河南道。
In the first year of Taichang he was promoted to censor. At that time the Xizong Emperor ascended the throne while still young; there was no empress dowager above, and palace and court stood in peril and uncertainty. Huazhong submitted a memorial impeaching Assisting Minister Fang Congzhe; the throne acknowledged receipt. In the second month of the first year of Tianqi he memorialized on eight worrying trends of the times: inner-palace discipline gradually slackening, the remonstrance path gradually devalued, law and discipline gradually decaying, bribery gradually conspicuous, the frontier gradually deteriorating, official responsibilities gradually lost, eunuchs gradually growing powerful, and hearts gradually turning away. His words were all trenchant and to the point. He was dispatched to inspect Xuanfu and Datong, then returned home to observe mourning. After the mourning period ended, he was recalled to oversee the Henan circuit as censor.
65
杨涟劾魏忠贤，化中亦率同官上疏曰：“忠贤障日蔽月，逞威作福，视大臣如奴隶，斥言官若孤雏，杀内廷外廷如草菅。 朝野共危，神人胥愤，特陛下未之知，故忠贤犹有畏心。 今涟已侃词入告矣，陛下念潜邸微劳，或贷忠贤以不死。 而忠贤实自惧一死，惧死之念深，将挺而走险，骑虎难下，臣恐其横逞之毒不在搢绅，而即在陛下。 陛下试思，深宫之内，可使多疑多惧之人日侍左右，而不为防制哉？ ”疏入，忠贤大恨。
When Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian, Huazhong also led his colleagues in submitting a memorial: "Zhongxian blocks out sun and moon alike, flaunts his power and hoards favor for himself, treats chief ministers like slaves, drives remonstrating officials away like helpless fledglings, and kills men inside and outside the court as if they were worthless grass. Court and countryside alike are in peril, and gods and men share the outrage. Only because Your Majesty has not yet learned of this does Zhongxian still retain some fear. Lian has already submitted his accusation to the throne. Your Majesty, recalling Zhongxian's minor service during the years in the hidden residence, may be inclined to spare him from death. Yet Zhongxian truly fears for his own life. The deeper that fear runs, the more likely he is to lash out in desperation—once astride a tiger, he cannot climb down. I fear his unrestrained cruelty will strike not at the officials but at Your Majesty himself. Consider, Your Majesty: within the inner palace, can a man so suspicious and fearful be allowed to attend you daily without any guard or restraint? When the memorial reached the throne, Zhongxian hated him bitterly.
66
锦衣陈居恭者，忠贤爪牙也，为涟所论及，亦攻忠贤自解。 化中特疏劾之，落其职。 毛文龙献俘十二人，而稚儿童女居其八。 化中力请释之，因言文龙叙功之滥。 忠贤素庇文龙，益不悦。 崔呈秀按淮、扬，赃私狼籍，回道考核，化中据实上之，崔呈秀大恨。 会谢应祥廷推被讦，化中与其事，呈秀遂嗾忠贤贬化中秩，调之外。 已，窜入汪文言狱词中，逮下诏狱。 呈秀令许显纯坐以杨镐、熊廷弼贿六千，酷刑拷掠，于狱中毙之。 崇祯初，赠太仆卿，官其一子。 福王时，追谥忠愍。
Chen Jugong of the Brocade Guard was one of Zhongxian's henchmen. Because Lian's memorial had also implicated him, he attacked Zhongxian as well in order to clear himself. Huazhong submitted a separate memorial impeaching him, and Chen was stripped of his post. Mao Wenlong presented twelve captives, eight of whom were young children and girls. Huazhong strongly petitioned for their release and denounced the extravagance of Wenlong's claims of merit. Zhongxian had long shielded Wenlong and was all the more displeased. When Cui Chengxiu inspected Huai and Yang, his corruption was flagrant. On his return from circuit and during the performance review, Huazhong reported the facts truthfully, and Chengxiu hated him bitterly. When Xie Yingxiang was impeached during the metropolitan recommendation process, Huazhong was involved in the case. Chengxiu then incited Zhongxian to reduce Huazhong's rank and transfer him out of the capital. Soon his name was inserted into Wang Wuyan's prison testimony, and he was seized and sent to the imperial prison.
