Chengxiu had Xu Xianchun convict him of taking six thousand taels in bribes from Yang Hao and Xiong Tingbi. Under brutal torture he was beaten to death in prison. At the start of the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud, and one son was granted office. Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously given the title Loyal and Lamented.
67
顾大章，字伯钦，常熟人。 父云程，南京太常卿。 大章与弟大韶，孪生子也。 大章举万历三十五年进士，授泉州推官，乞改常州教授。 父丧除，值朝中朋党角立，正士日摧。 大章慨然曰：“昔贾彪不入‘顾’‘厨’之目，卒西行以解其难。 余向与东林疏，可以彪自况也。 ”乃入都，补国子博士。 与朝士通往来，阴察其交关肯綮，清流赖之。
Gu Dazhang, whose style name was Bojin, came from Changshu. His father Yuncheng served as Minister of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing. Dazhang and his younger brother Dashao were twins. Dazhang passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-fifth year of the Wanli reign, was appointed investigating censor of Quanzhou, and requested transfer to instructor at Changzhou. After his father's mourning period ended, factional parties in court stood locked in opposition, and upright men were worn down day by day. Dazhang said with feeling: "In the past Jia Biao was not counted among the 'Gu' and 'Chu' factions, yet in the end he went west to resolve their crisis. I have long kept my distance from the Donglin faction; I may compare myself to Biao." Thereupon he entered the capital and was appointed Doctor of the Imperial Academy. He kept in contact with court officials, secretly observing the vital points of their alliances; the Clear Stream faction relied on him.
68
稍迁刑部主事。 以奉使归。 还朝，天启已改元，进员外郎。 尚书王纪令署山东司事。 司辖辇毂，最难任。 自辽阳失，五城及京营巡捕日以逻奸细为事，稍有踪迹，率论死。 绝无左验者二百余人，所司莫敢谳，多徙官去，囚未死者仅四之一。 大章言于纪曰：“以一身易五十人命且甘之，矧一官乎！ ”即日会谳，系三人，余悉移大理释放。 纪大嗟服。 佟卜年之狱，纪用大章言拟流卜年，未上而纪斥。 侍郎杨东明署事，欲置之大辟，大章力争，卒拟流。 忤旨，诘责，竟论卜年辟，瘐死狱中。
He was gradually promoted to section director in the Ministry of Justice. He returned after completing an imperial mission. On returning to court, the Tianqi reign had already been inaugurated, and he was promoted to vice director. Minister Wang Ji ordered him to take charge of the Shandong Bureau. That bureau had jurisdiction over the imperial capital region—the hardest post to fill. Since the fall of Liaoyang, the Five Cities and the capital garrison patrols had made daily work of hunting spies; the slightest trace usually led to a death sentence. More than two hundred men had absolutely no corroborating evidence, yet the responsible offices dared not hold joint review. Many officials transferred away, and only one in four of the prisoners remained alive. Dazhang said to Ji: "To trade one life for fifty others one would still gladly do it—how much more for one official post! That same day he convened joint review, detained three men, and had all the rest transferred to the Court of Judicial Review for release. Ji sighed in deep admiration. In the case of Tong Bunian, Ji, following Dazhang's advice, drafted a sentence of exile for Bunian, but before it was submitted Ji was dismissed. Vice Minister Yang Dongming took charge of affairs and wished to impose the death penalty, but Dazhang argued forcefully, and in the end exile was proposed. Defying the imperial will, Dazhang was reprimanded; in the end Bunian was sentenced to death and died of illness in prison.
69
魏忠贤欲借刘一献株累刘一燝，大章力辨其非，忠贤大恨。 卜年、一献事具《纪》、《一燝传》中。 熊廷弼、王化贞之下吏也，法司诸属二十八人共谳，多有议宽廷弼者。 大章因援“议能”、“议劳”例，言化贞宜诛，廷弼宜论戍。 然二人卒坐死。 大章亦迁兵部去，无异议也。 会王纪劾罢徐大化，又疏刺客氏，其党疑纪疏出大章手，恨之。 大化令所亲御史杨维垣讦大章妄倡“八议”，鬻大狱，大章疏辨。 维垣四疏力攻，言纳廷弼贿四万，且列其鬻狱数事，反覆诋讦不休。 大章危甚，赖座主叶向高保持之，下所司验问，都御史孙玮等白其诬。 帝以大章渎辨，稍夺其俸，大章遂引归。
Wei Zhongxian wished to use Liu Yixian to implicate Liu Yijin, but Dazhang forcefully argued that this was wrong, and Zhongxian hated him deeply. The cases of Bunian and Yixian are fully recorded in the biographies of Wang Ji and Liu Yijin. Xiong Tingbi and Wang Huazhen had been sent down to the judiciary; twenty-eight officials of the legal offices jointly reviewed the case, and many argued for leniency toward Tingbi. Dazhang therefore invoked the precedents of "debating merit" and "debating service," arguing that Huazhen deserved execution while Tingbi deserved exile. Yet in the end both men were sentenced to death. Dazhang also transferred to the Ministry of War and departed without objection. When Wang Ji impeached and drove out Xu Dahua, and also submitted a memorial attacking Ke Shi, their faction suspected Ji's memorial had come from Dazhang's hand and hated him for it. Dahua had his trusted censor Yang Weiyuan impeach Dazhang for recklessly advocating the "Eight Debates" and selling major cases; Dazhang submitted a memorial in his defense. Weiyuan forcefully attacked in four memorials, saying Dazhang had taken forty thousand taels in bribes from Tingbi and listing several instances of selling cases, reviling and slandering him repeatedly without cease. Dazhang was in grave peril, but thanks to his patron Ye Xianggao protecting him, the matter was sent down to the responsible offices for verification, and Censor-in-Chief Sun Wei and others declared the charges false. The emperor deemed Dazhang's defense insolent and partially suspended his salary; Dazhang thereupon resigned and returned home.
70
五年起官。 历礼部郎中，陕西副使。 大化已起大理丞，与维垣为忠贤鹰犬，因假汪文言狱连及大章，逮下镇抚拷掠，坐赃四万。 及杨涟等五人既死，群小聚谋，谓诸人潜毙于狱，无以厌人心，宜付法司定罪，明诏天下。 乃移大章刑部狱，由是涟等惨死状外人始闻。 比对簿，大章词气不挠。 刑部尚书李养正等一如镇抚原词，以“移宫”事牵合封疆，坐六人大辟。 爰书既上，忠贤大喜，矫诏布告四方，仍移大章镇抚。 大章慨然曰：“吾安可再入此狱！ ”呼酒与大韶诀，趣和药饮之，不死，投缳而卒。 崇祯初，赠太仆卿，官其一子。 福王时，追谥裕愍。
In the fifth year he was recalled to office. He successively served as section director in the Ministry of Rites and vice commissioner of Shaanxi. Dahua had already been recalled as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review; together with Weiyuan he served as Zhongxian's hunting dogs. Using Wang Wuyan's case as a pretext, they implicated Dazhang, seized him, sent him to the Brocade Guard prison for torture, and convicted him of embezzling forty thousand taels. After Yang Lian and four others had died, the petty men gathered in counsel, saying that since the men had been secretly killed in prison, this could not satisfy public opinion; the cases should be turned over to the legal offices for judgment and proclaimed to the realm by imperial edict. Dazhang was then moved to the Ministry of Justice prison, and from this the outside world first learned of the cruel deaths of Lian and the others. When confronted with the prison register, Dazhang's words and bearing did not waver. Minister of Justice Li Yangzheng and the others followed the Brocade Guard's original testimony exactly, linking the Transfer of the Palace affair with frontier affairs, and convicted all six men of capital crimes. Once the final judgment was submitted, Zhongxian rejoiced greatly, forged an edict proclaiming it to the four quarters, and still transferred Dazhang back to the Brocade Guard prison. Dazhang said with feeling: "How can I enter this prison again! He called for wine to take leave of Dashao, hurried to mix poison and drink it; when he did not die, he hanged himself and expired. At the start of the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud, and one son was granted office. Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously given the title Generous and Lamented.
71
初，大章等被逮，秘狱中忽生黄芝，光彩远映。 及六人毕入，适成六瓣，或以为祥。 大章叹曰：“芝，瑞物也，而辱于此，吾辈其有幸乎？ ”已而果然。
At first, when Dazhang and the others were seized, a yellow fungus suddenly sprang up in the secret prison, its radiance shining far. When all six men had entered, it happened to form six petals; some took it as an auspicious sign. Dazhang sighed: "The fungus is an auspicious thing, yet it appears here in disgrace—can we be fortunate? And so it proved.
72
大韶，字仲恭，老于诸生。 通经史百家及内典，于《诗》、《礼》、《仪礼》、《周官》多所发明，他辨驳者复数万言。 尝以为宋、元以来述者之事备，学者但当诵而不述，将死，始缮所笺《诗》、《礼》、《庄子》，曰《炳烛斋随笔》云。
Dashao, whose style name was Zhonggong, was a veteran among students. He mastered the classics, histories, the hundred schools, and Buddhist scriptures; on the Book of Songs, Book of Rites, Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial, and Rites of Zhou he made many original insights, and his other critiques and rebuttals ran to tens of thousands of words. He once held that since the Song and Yuan dynasties writers' work had been fully done, scholars need only recite and not compose new writings. Near death he finally compiled his commentaries on the Book of Songs, Book of Rites, and Zhuangzi, titled Collected Jottings from the Bright Candle Studio.
73
王之寀，字心一，朝邑人。 万历二十九年进士。 除清苑知县，迁刑部主事。
Wang Zhicai, whose style name was Xinyi, came from Chaoyi. He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-ninth year of the Wanli reign. He was appointed magistrate of Qingyuan and promoted to section director in the Ministry of Justice.
74
四十三年五月初四日酉刻，有不知姓名男子，持枣木梃入慈庆宫门，击伤守门内侍李鉴。 至前殿檐下，为内侍韩本用等所执，付东华门守卫指挥硃雄等收之。 慈庆宫者，皇太子所居宫也。 明日，皇太子奏闻，帝命法司按问。 巡皇城御史刘廷元鞫奏：“犯名张差，蓟州人。 止称吃斋讨封，语无伦次。 按其迹，若涉疯癫，稽其貌，实系黠猾。 请下法司严讯。 ”时东宫虽久定，帝待之薄。 中外疑郑贵妃与其弟国泰谋危太子，顾未得事端，而方从哲辈亦颇关通戚畹以自固。 差被执，举朝惊骇，廷元以疯癫奏。 刑部山东司郎中胡士相偕员外郎赵会桢、劳永嘉共讯，一如廷元指。 言：“差积柴草，为人所烧，气愤发癫。 于四月内诉冤入京，遇不知名男子二人，绐令执梃作冤状。 乃由东华门入，直至慈庆宫门。 按律当斩，加等立决。 ”稿定未上。 山东司主治京师事，署印侍郎张问达以属之。 而士相、永嘉与廷元皆浙人，士相又廷元姻也，疯癫具狱，之寀心疑其非。
On the fourth day of the fifth month of the forty-third year, at the you hour, an unnamed man carrying a jujube-wood club entered the gate of Ciqing Palace and struck and wounded the gatekeeper eunuch Li Jian. Reaching the eaves of the front hall, he was seized by the eunuchs Han Benyong and others and handed over to the Donghua Gate guard commander Zhu Xiong and others for custody. Ciqing Palace was the palace where the crown prince resided. The next day the crown prince reported the matter, and the emperor ordered the legal offices to investigate. Censor Liu Tingyuan, patrolling the Imperial City, interrogated and reported: "The culprit is named Zhang Cha, a man of Jizhou. He only spoke of fasting and seeking enfeoffment; his words were incoherent. Judging by his conduct he seemed deranged, but examining his appearance, he was in fact sly and cunning. I request that he be sent down to the legal offices for strict interrogation." At that time, though the Eastern Palace had long been settled, the emperor treated the heir coolly. Inside and outside the court there was suspicion that Consort Zheng and her brother Guotai plotted to endanger the crown prince, but no clear incident had yet appeared; Fang Congzhe and his sort also maintained ties with imperial consorts' kin to secure themselves. When Cha was seized, the whole court was shocked; Tingyuan reported derangement. Section chief Hu Shixiang of the Shandong Bureau in the Ministry of Justice, together with vice directors Zhao Huizhen and Lao Yongjia, jointly interrogated him, exactly as Tingyuan had indicated. They reported: "Cha had piled firewood that someone burned; in anger he went mad. Within the fourth month he came to the capital to voice his grievance; he met two unnamed men who deceived him into taking a club and staging a grievance petition. He then entered through the Donghua Gate and reached straight to the gate of Ciqing Palace. By law he should be decapitated; with the additional grade, immediate execution. The draft judgment was fixed but not yet submitted. The Shandong Bureau chiefly handled capital affairs; Vice Minister Zhang Wenda, holding the seal in charge, delegated the matter to them. Shixiang and Yongjia, like Tingyuan, were all men of Zhejiang; Shixiang was moreover Tingyuan's in-law by marriage. The completed verdict of derangement made Zhicai suspect it was false.
75
是月十一日，之寀值提牢散饭狱中，末至差，私诘其实。 初言“告状”，复言“凉死罢，已无用”。 之寀令置饭差前：“吐实与饭，否则饿死。 ”麾左右出，留二吏扶问之。 始言：“小名张五儿。 有马三舅、李外父令随不知姓名一老公，说事成与汝地几亩。 比至京，入不知街道大宅子。 一老公饭我云：‘汝先冲一遭，遇人辄打死，死了我们救汝。 ’畀我枣木棍，导我由后宰门直至宫门上，击门者堕地。 老公多，遂被执。 ”之寀备揭其语，因问达以闻。 且言差不癫不狂，有心有胆。 乞缚凶犯于文华殿前朝审，或敕九卿科道三法司会问。 疏入未下，大理丞王士昌、行人司正陆大受、户部主事张庭、给事中姚永济等连上疏趣之。 而大受疏有“奸戚”二字，帝恶之，与之寀疏俱不报。 廷元复请速检诸疏，下法司讯断。 御史过庭训言祸生肘腋，宜亟翦，亦俱不报。 庭训遂移文蓟州踪迹之。 知州戚延龄具言其致癫始末，言：“贵妃遣珰建佛寺，珰置陶造甓，居民多鬻薪获利者。 差卖田贸薪往市于珰，土人忌之，焚其薪。 差讼于珰，为所责，不胜愤，持梃欲告御状。 ”于是原问诸臣据为口实矣。
On the eleventh day of that month, Zhicai happened to be on duty distributing prisoners' meals in the jail; when he reached Cha last, he privately pressed him for the truth. At first Cha said "to lodge a complaint"; then he said "might as well die coolly—it's no use now." Zhicai ordered food placed before Cha: "Tell the truth and you get food; otherwise you starve. He waved his attendants out and kept two clerks to support and question him. Cha then began: "My pet name is Zhang Wu'er. My maternal uncle Ma and my father-in-law Li had me follow an unnamed old eunuch, saying that when the deed was done you would get several mu of land. When we reached the capital, we entered a great mansion on an unknown street. One eunuch fed me and said: "You go charge in first; whenever you meet someone, just beat them to death—we'll save you if you die. He gave me a jujube-wood club, led me from the Rear Butcher Gate straight to the palace gate, and those I struck at the gate fell to the ground. There were many eunuchs, so I was seized. Zhicai fully recorded his words and reported them through Wenda to inform the throne. He also said that Cha was not quite mad or deranged—he had purpose and courage. He begged that the murderous culprit be bound and tried at court before the Hall of Literary Glory, or that the emperor command the Nine Ministers, the censorate, and the Three Judicial Offices to sit in joint session. The memorial entered but no reply came down; Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Wang Shichang, Chief of the Reception Bureau Lu Dashou, Section Director of the Ministry of Revenue Zhang Ting, and Censor Yao Yongji and others submitted memorials in succession urging action. But Dashou's memorial contained the two characters "treacherous consort kin," which the emperor hated, and neither his nor Zhicai's memorial received reply. Tingyuan again requested that all memorials be quickly examined and the matter sent down to the legal offices for interrogation and judgment. Censor Guo Tingxun said disaster was springing from the emperor's armpit and should be swiftly cut off—all likewise received no reply. Tingxun then sent an official dispatch to Jizhou to trace the matter. Magistrate Qi Yanling recounted in full the whole course that had made Cha deranged, saying: "The Noble Consort sent eunuchs to build a Buddhist temple; the eunuchs set up pottery to make bricks, and many residents sold firewood for profit. Cha sold his fields to buy firewood and take it to market with the eunuchs; local people resented this and burned his firewood. Cha brought suit against the eunuchs and was rebuked by them; unable to bear his anger, he took a club intending to lodge an imperial petition. Thus the officials who had first questioned him took this as their talking point.
76
二十一日，刑部会十三司司官胡士相、陆梦龙、邹绍光、曾曰唯、赵会祯、劳永嘉、王之寀、吴养源、曾之可、柯文、罗光鼎、曾道唯、刘继礼、吴孟登、岳骏声、唐嗣美、马德沣、硃瑞凤等再审。 差供：“马三舅名三道，李外父名守才，不知姓名老公乃修铁瓦殿之庞保，不知街道宅子乃住朝外大宅之刘成。 二人令我打上宫门，打得小爷，吃有，著有。 ”小爷者，内监所称皇太子者也。 又言：“有姊夫孔道同谋，凡五人。 ”于是刑部行蓟州道，提马三道等，疏请法司提庞保、刘成对鞫，而给事中何士晋与从哲等亦俱以为言。 帝乃谕究主使，会法司拟罪。 是日，刑部据蓟州回文以上。 已，复谕严刑鞫审，速正典刑。 时中外籍籍，语多侵国泰，国泰出揭自白。 士晋复疏攻国泰，语具《士晋传》。
On the twenty-first day, the Ministry of Justice convened the officials of the Thirteen Bureaus—Hu Shixiang, Lu Menglong, Zou Shaoguang, Zeng Yuewei, Zhao Huizhen, Lao Yongjia, Wang Zhicai, Wu Yangyuan, Zeng Zhi'ke, Ke Wen, Luo Guangding, Zeng Daowei, Liu Jili, Wu Mengdeng, Yue Junsheng, Tang Simei, Ma Defeng, Zhu Ruifeng, and others—for re-examination. Cha testified: "My maternal uncle Ma is named Sandao; my father-in-law Li is named Shoucai; the unnamed old eunuch is Pang Bao, who was repairing the Iron-Tile Hall; the unknown-street mansion is the great residence outside the court where Liu Cheng lives. The two men ordered me to strike at the palace gate; I struck the Young Master. They promised food and clothing. "The Young Master" is what the eunuchs call the crown prince. He also said: "My brother-in-law Kong Dao was an accomplice—five men in all. Then the Ministry of Justice dispatched orders through the Jizhou circuit to summon Ma Sandao and the others, and memorialized requesting the legal offices to summon Pang Bao and Liu Cheng for joint interrogation; Censor He Shijin and Congzhe and others also all spoke likewise. The emperor then ordered investigation of the mastermind and directed the legal offices to draft sentences. That day the Ministry of Justice submitted the reply document from Jizhou upward. Soon after, he again ordered strict interrogation under torture and swift execution according to law. At the time rumor swirled inside and outside the court, much of it touching Guotai; Guotai issued a public statement to clear himself. Shijin again submitted a memorial attacking Guotai—the details are in his biography.
77
先是，百户王曰乾上变，言奸人孔学等为巫蛊，将不利于皇太子，词已连刘成。 成与保皆贵妃宫中内侍也。 至是，复涉成。 帝心动，谕贵妃善为计。 贵妃窘，乞哀皇太子，自明无它； 帝亦数慰谕，俾太子白之廷臣。 太子亦以事连贵妃，大惧，乃缘帝及贵妃意，期速结。 二十八日，帝亲御慈宁宫，皇太子侍御座右，三皇孙雁行立左阶下。 召大学士方从哲、吴道南暨文武诸臣入，责以离间父子，谕令磔张差、庞保、刘成，无他及。 因执太子手曰：“此儿极孝，我极爱惜。 ”既又手约太子体，谕曰：“自襁褓养成丈夫，使我有别意，何不早更置？ 且福王已之国，去此数千里，自非宣召，能翼而至乎？ ”因命内侍引三皇孙至石级上，令诸臣熟视，曰：“朕诸孙俱长成，更何说？ ”顾问皇太子有何语，与诸臣悉言无隐。 皇太子具言：“疯癫之人宜速决，毋株连。 ”又责诸臣云：“我父子何等亲爱，而外廷议论纷如，尔等为无君之臣，使我为不孝之子。 ”帝又谓诸臣曰：“尔等听皇太子语否？ ”复连声重申之。 诸臣跪听，叩头出，遂命法司决差。 明日磔于市。 又明日，司礼监会廷臣鞫保、成于文华门。 时已无左证，保、成展转不承。 会太子传谕轻拟，廷臣乃散去。 越十余日，刑部议流马三道、李守才、孔道。 帝从之，而毙保、成于内廷。 其事遂止。
Earlier, Company Commander Wang Yuegan had submitted an extraordinary memorial, saying that the villain Kong Xue and others practiced witchcraft and sorcery intending harm to the crown prince; the testimony had already implicated Liu Cheng. Cheng and Bao were both inner attendants in the Noble Consort's palace. At this point, Cheng was again implicated. The emperor's heart was moved; he instructed the Noble Consort to plan well. The Noble Consort was cornered; she begged mercy from the crown prince and declared she had no other intent; The emperor also repeatedly comforted and instructed her, having the crown prince explain this to the court officials. The crown prince also, since the affair touched the Noble Consort, was greatly afraid; he therefore followed the emperor's and the Noble Consort's intent, hoping for a swift conclusion. On the twenty-eighth day the emperor personally attended at Cining Palace; the crown prince attended at his right hand, and the three imperial grandsons stood in file like geese on the left steps below. He summoned Grand Secretaries Fang Congzhe and Wu Daonan, together with civil and military officials, rebuked them for driving apart father and son, and ordered that Zhang Cha, Pang Bao, and Liu Cheng be dismembered, with no further scope of punishment. Taking the crown prince's hand he said: "This son is utterly filial; I cherish him utterly. Then, taking the crown prince's body in his hands, he instructed: "Raised from swaddling clothes to a grown man—if I had other intentions, why not have replaced him long ago? Moreover the Prince of Fu has already gone to his fief, thousands of li from here—unless expressly summoned, could he fly here on wings? He then ordered inner attendants to lead the three imperial grandsons to the stone steps, had the officials look closely, and said: "All my grandsons have grown up—what more is there to say? He asked what the crown prince had to say and told the officials to speak without concealment. The crown prince stated in full: "The deranged man should be swiftly disposed of—do not implicate others. He also rebuked the officials: "How close my father and I are—yet outside the court discussion swirls; you are ministers without a lord, making me an unfilial son. The emperor again said to the officials: "Do you hear the crown prince's words? He repeatedly reaffirmed this, again and again. The officials knelt listening, kowtowed, and withdrew; he then ordered the legal offices to execute Cha. The next day Cha was dismembered in the marketplace. The day after, the Directorate of Ceremonial, together with court officials, interrogated Bao and Cheng at the Wenhua Gate. By then there was no corroborating evidence; Bao and Cheng repeatedly denied the charges. When the crown prince transmitted an instruction for lenient sentencing, the court officials then dispersed. More than ten days later the Ministry of Justice proposed banishment for Ma Sandao, Li Shoucai, and Kong Dao. The emperor agreed, and had Bao and Cheng executed within the inner court. The affair then came to a stop.
78
当是时，帝不见群臣二十有五年矣，以之寀发保、成事，特一出以释群臣疑，且调剂贵妃、太子。 念其事似有迹，故不遽罪之寀也。 四十五年京察，给事中徐绍吉、御史韩浚用拾遗劾之寀贪，遂削其籍。
At that time the emperor had not seen his ministers for twenty-five years; because Zhicai had exposed the affair of Bao and Cheng, he made a special appearance to dispel the ministers' suspicions and to balance matters between the Noble Consort and the crown prince. Reflecting that the affair seemed to have substance, he did not immediately punish Zhicai. In the capital evaluation of the forty-fifth year, Censor-in-chief Xu Shaoji and Censor Han Jun used the remembrancer mechanism to impeach Zhicai for greed, and his name was struck from the rolls.
79
天启初，廷臣多为之讼冤，召复故官。 二年二月上《复仇疏》，曰：
At the start of the Tianqi reign many court officials petitioned on his behalf to clear his name, and he was recalled to his former office. In the second year, second month, he submitted a Memorial on Vengeance, saying:
80
《礼》，君父之仇，不共戴天。 齐襄公复九世之仇，《春秋》大之。 曩李选侍气殴圣母，陛下再三播告中外，停其贵妃之封，圣母在天之灵必有心安而目瞑者。 此复仇一大义也。
The Book of Rites says: "A lord's or father's enemy—you do not live under the same heaven with him." Duke Xiang of Qi avenged a nine-generations-old feud; the Spring and Autumn Annals honors this. Formerly Lady Li, the appointed consort, struck and abused the Empress Dowager in a fit of rage; Your Majesty repeatedly proclaimed this inside and outside the court and suspended her enfeoffment as Noble Consort—the Empress Dowager's spirit in heaven must surely be at peace and close her eyes content. This is a great principle of vengeance.
81
乃先帝一生遭逢多难，弥留之际，饮恨以崩。 试问：李可灼之误用药，引进者谁？ 崔文升之故用药，主使者谁？ 恐方从哲之罪不在可灼、文升下。 此先帝大仇未复者，一也。
Yet the late emperor encountered many hardships throughout his life, and at his last breath departed bearing resentment. Consider: Li Kezhuo's mistaken administration of medicine—who introduced him? Cui Wensheng's deliberate administration of medicine—who was the mastermind? I fear Fang Congzhe's guilt is no less than Kezhuo's or Wensheng's. This is one great unrevenged wrong against the late emperor.
82
张差持梃犯宫，安危止在呼吸。 此乾坤何等时，乃刘廷元曲盖奸谋，以疯癫具狱矣。 胡士相等改注口语，以卖薪成招矣。 其后复谳，差供同谋举事，内外设伏多人。 守才、三道亦供结党连谋，而士相辈悉抹去之。 当时有内应，有外援。 一夫作难，九庙震惊，何物凶徒，敢肆行不道乃尔！ 缘外戚郑国泰私结刘廷元、刘光复、姚宗文辈，珠玉金钱充满其室。 言官结舌，莫敢谁何，遂无复顾惮，睥睨神器耳。 国泰虽死，罪不容诛。 法当开棺戮尸，夷其族，赭其宫，而至今犹未议及。 此先帝大仇未复者，二也。
Zhang Cha carrying a club violated the palace; safety and peril hung by a breath. What a moment for heaven and earth—and Liu Tingyuan bent over to cover the conspiracy, completing the case as derangement. Hu Shixiang and others altered and annotated the spoken testimony, making the selling-firewood story into a confession. Later, on re-examination, Cha testified to conspiracy and joint action, with many men posted inside and outside as ambush. Shoucai and Sandao also testified to forming a faction and plotting together, but Shixiang and his sort erased all of this. At the time there were inside accomplices and outside support. One man raised trouble and the Nine Temples trembled—what sort of murderous villain dares act so lawlessly! Because the consort kin Zheng Guotai privately bonded with Liu Tingyuan, Liu Guangfu, Yao Zongwen, and their sort, pearls, jade, and gold filled their rooms. Censors clammed up and dared not challenge them; thus they no longer feared restraint and cast sidelong glances at the imperial throne. Guotai though dead—the crime could not be pardoned by death alone. By law his coffin should be opened and his corpse dismembered, his clan exterminated, his residence red-marked for confiscation—yet to this day none of this has even been discussed. This is the second great unrevenged wrong against the late emperor.
83
总之，用药之术，即梃击之谋。 击不中而促之药，是文升之药惨于张差之梃也。 张差之前，从无张差； 刘成之后，岂乏刘成？ 臣见陛下之孤立于上矣。 又言：
In sum, the art of administering medicine is the same plot as the club assault. The blow did not land, so they hastened the medicine—Wensheng's medicine was more grievous than Cha's club. Before Zhang Cha there had never been a Zhang Cha; After Liu Cheng, can Liu Chengs be lacking? I see Your Majesty standing alone above. He also said:
84
郎中胡士相等，主疯癫者也。 堂官张问达，调停疯癫者也。 寺臣王士昌疏忠而心佞，评无只字，讼多溢词。 堂官张问达语转而意圆，先允疯癫，后宽奸宄。 劳永嘉、岳骏声等同恶相济。 张差招有“三十六头儿”，则胡士相阁笔； 招有“东边一起干事”，则岳骏声言波及无辜； 招有“红封票，高真人”，则劳永嘉言不及究红封教。 今高一奎见监蓟州，系镇朔卫人。 盖高一奎，主持红封教者也； 马三道，管给红票者也； 庞保、刘成，供给红封教多人撒棍者也。 诸奸增减会审公单，大逆不道。
Section chief Hu Shixiang and others advocated the derangement theory. Department head Zhang Wenda mediated toward derangement. Court official Wang Shichang's memorial was loyal in appearance but treacherous at heart—judgment without a single honest word, litigation full of excess rhetoric. Department head Zhang Wenda's words turned but his meaning circled round—first conceding derangement, later lenient toward the villainous conspirators. Lao Yongjia, Yue Junsheng, and others aided one another in evil. When Cha's confession mentioned "thirty-six leaders," Hu Shixiang laid down his brush; When it mentioned "doing things together on the east side," Yue Junsheng said the innocent would be implicated; When it mentioned "red-sealed tickets, Master Gao," Lao Yongjia said they need not pursue the Red Seal Teaching. Now Gao Yikui is imprisoned in Jizhou; he is a man of Zhenshuo Guard. Gao Yikui, in fact, ran the Red Seal Teaching; Ma Sandao distributed the red tickets; Pang Bao and Liu Cheng supplied many men of the Red Seal Teaching with clubs. The conspirators added to and subtracted from the joint examination record—treason beyond measure.
85
疏入，帝不问，而先主疯癫者恨次骨。
The memorial entered; the emperor made no inquiry, but those who had first advocated derangement hated Zhicai to the bone.
86
未几，之寀迁尚宝少卿。 逾年，迁太仆少卿，寻转本寺卿。 廷元及岳骏声、曾道唯以之寀侵己，先后疏辨。 之寀亦连疏力折，并发诸人前议差狱时，分金红庙中，及居间主名甚悉。 事虽不行，诸人益疾之。
Before long Zhicai was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Treasures. The following year he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud, and soon after became director of that court. Tingyuan, Yue Junsheng, and Zeng Daowei, believing Zhicai had attacked them, submitted memorials one after another in self-defense. Zhicai answered with a series of forceful memorials, exposing how the others had earlier met to fix the verdict, divided bribes in the Red Temple, and naming in detail every intermediary involved. Though his charges did not prevail, his enemies hated him all the more.
87
四年秋，拜刑部右侍郎。 明年二月，魏忠贤势大张，其党杨维垣首翻“梃击”之案，力诋之寀，坐除名。 俄入之汪文言狱中，下抚按提问。 岳骏声复讦之，且言其逼取郑国泰二万金，有诏追治。 及修《三朝要典》，其“梃击”事以之寀为罪首。 府尹刘志选复重劾之，遂逮下诏狱，坐赃八千，之寀竟瘐死。 崇祯初，复官，赐恤。
In the autumn of the fourth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice. In the second month of the following year Wei Zhongxian's power surged; his follower Yang Weiyuan led the effort to overturn the Assault at the Palace Gate verdict and fiercely attacked Zhicai, who was stripped of office. Soon he was swept into the Wang Wenyan case and interrogated under orders from the grand coordinator and regional inspector. Yue Junsheng denounced him again, claiming he had extorted twenty thousand taels from Zheng Guotai; the throne ordered a full prosecution. When the Essentials of Three Reigns was compiled, the Assault at the Palace Gate affair was written to make Zhicai the chief culprit. Prefect Liu Zhixuan impeached him again; he was arrested and sent to the imperial prison, convicted of embezzling eight thousand taels, and Zhicai died of illness in confinement. At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign his office was restored and posthumous honors were granted.
88
自“梃击”之议起，而“红丸”、“移宫”二事继之。 两党是非争胜，祸患相寻，迄明亡而后已。
Once debate over the Assault at the Palace Gate began, the Red Pills and Transfer of the Palace controversies followed. The two factions battled over right and wrong, calamity followed calamity, and the strife did not end until the dynasty fell.
89
赞曰：国之将亡也，先自戕其善类，而水旱盗贼乘之。 故祸乱之端，士君子恒先被其毒。 异哉，明之所称“三案”者！ 举朝士大夫喋喋不去口，而元恶大憝因用以剪除善类，卒致杨、左诸人身填牢户，与东汉季年若蹈一辙。 国安得不亡乎！
The commentator says: When a state is about to fall, it first destroys its own good men—and then flood, drought, and bandits rush in to finish the work. Thus at the outset of every calamity, gentlemen and scholars are always the first to suffer. How strange were the Ming's so-called Three Cases! Court scholars chattered about them without cease, yet the greatest villains used these affairs to purge the good, until Yang, Zuo, and their fellows filled the prisons—following the same road the Eastern Han had taken in its final years. How could the dynasty not fall!
